DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer's concern by operating the power seat(s) to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Seat tracks obstructed.

Seat at limit(s) of travel.

Damaged lumbar support hose.

Damaged lumbar support switch and valve.

Open 20A circuit breaker in fuse junction panel.

Open fuse junction panel fuse number 8, 15A.

Loose, corroded or damaged connectors.

Damaged switches.

Damaged motors.

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent, connected to the data 
link connector (DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) 
and to execute Self Test Diagnostics for the driver seat module and driver 
door module as outlined in Section 18-04 .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to Driver Seat 
Module (DDM) or Driver Door Module (DDM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index 
to continue diagnostics.

If the driver seat module or driver door module cannot be accessed by 
the New Generation Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent, go to Pinpoint Test C 
 for driver seat module 
or Pinpoint Test D for driver door
module.

Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) 
001-00001 or equivalent, may also be used to diagnose this system.

DTC B1517: SEAT OCCUPIED SWITCH SHORT TO BATTERY

 B1517-1 CHECK CIRCUIT 117 (W) 

Disconnect driver door module C2 connector.

Using a voltmeter, measure for voltage at driver door module Pin C2-8, 
Circuit 177 (W).

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to B1517-2 
 .

No

 .

Read PID D_SEAT.

 .

DTC B1663: DRIVER SEAT FRONT TILT OUTPUT CIRCUIT FAILURE

 NOTE: If DTC B1663, B1664, and B1665 are retrieved at the same time GO to Pinpoint Test A 
.

 B1663-1 RERUN TEST 

Turn ignition switch to RUN. 

Turn ignition switch OFF. These two steps "wake up" the driver seat 
module.

Open driver side door. This disables delay accessory function.

 NOTE: Seat will move a short distance in each direction during self-test.

Execute self-test.

Inspect seat track and make sure that all obstructions are removed.

Rerun self-test.

 Is DTC B1663 still present?

Yes

No

GO to B1663-2 
 .

SYSTEM operating normally.

 Are DTCs B1664 and B1665 also set?

Yes

No

GO to Pinpoint Test B .

GO to B1663-3 
 .

 B1663-3 TEST MOTORS 

Press driver seat front up switch for 2 seconds.

Press driver seat front down switch for 2 seconds.

 Does motor move for 1 second, then stop before switch is released?

Yes

No

GO to B1663-4 
 .

SERVICE both Circuits 979 (R/LB) and 990 (Y/LB) to motor for open

 B1663-4 TEST POTENTIOMETER FEEDBACK FOR OPEN 

Using a voltmeter, carefully back probe front up/down potentiometer

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat, Driver or Passenger�Power Seat

 Removal and Installation 

 NOTE: If some of the removal and installation steps do not apply to the 
particular vehicle being serviced, proceed to the next step and review the 
appropriate illustrations shown. Unless otherwise noted, the illustrations 
shown are typical of split bench front seat assemblies, arm rests (front and 
rear), and rear seat cushion and back assemblies.

Remove front seat track to floor insulators (61748) (if equipped) to 
expose nuts and washers and/or bolts. 

Remove nuts and washers and/or bolts retaining seat track assembly to 
front floor pan (11135). 

Lift the seat up enough to disconnect the seat harness connector and 
disconnect connector (if so equipped). Remove the seat and track assembly from 
the vehicle. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten the retaining bolts and 
the outboard nut to 17-23 Nm (13-16 lb-ft). Tighten the 
inboard nut to 68-92 Nm (51-67 lb-ft).

 Removal and Installation 

 CAUTION: Use care when handling seat and track assembly. Dropping assembly or

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat, Rear Bench

 Removal 

Apply knee pressure to the lower front portion of rear seat cushion 
assembly. Push rearward to disengage rear seat cushion pad and frame (600A88) 
from rear seat cushion front retainers (63370). 

Remove the rear safety belt retractor and tongue (611B68) and rear seat 
back pad and frame lower retaining nuts. 

Grasp the seat back assembly at the bottom and lift up to disengage the 
hanger wire from the retainer brackets. 

Remove the seat back assembly from the vehicle. 

 Rear Bench Seat 

[FIGURE: R6569C.gif]

 Installation 

Position the seat back assembly into the vehicle so that the hanger 
wire is engaged with the retaining brackets. 

Install the rear safety belt retractor and tongue and rear seat back 
pad and frame retainer nuts. Tighten to 40-55 Nm (30-41 
lb-ft). 

Position the seat cushion assembly into the vehicle. 

Apply knee pressure to the lower portion of the seat cushion assembly. 
Push rearward and down to lock the rear seat cushion pad and frame into 
position. 

Check rear seat cushion pad and frame to make sure it is secured into 
rear seat cushion front retainer.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat Track

 Manual 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove seat and seat track as outlined.

Place the seat and track assembly upside down on a clean bench.

 NOTE: To ease front seat track assist spring (61828) removal and 
installation, adjust seat to full forward position.

Disconnect front seat track assist spring.

Remove the seat track-to-front seat cushion frame and spring retaining 
screws and remove the seat track assembly.

If the seat track is being replaced, transfer the front seat cushion 
extension handle (603A86) to the new seat track assembly.

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten the seat track-to-front 
seat cushion frame and spring retaining screws to 17-23 Nm 
(13-16 lb-ft).

 Removal and Installation

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat Regulator Control Switch 

 Power�Six-Way 

 Removal and Installation 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Gently pry up on the front of the window regulator switch housing 
(14527). 

Unhook rear edge of window regulator switch housing and remove window 
regulator switch housing from front door trim panel (23942). 

Remove two screws retaining electrical connector to window regulator 
switch housing. 

Carefully pry seat regulator control switch (14A701) from connector 
with a small screwdriver. Take care not to damage the connector pins. 

To install, position seat regulator control switch to connector and 
carefully press into place. 

To complete installation, reverse Removal procedure. 

 Programmable Memory 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove one inside door handle cup retaining screw. Using a screwdriver, 
disengage retaining studs from front door trim panel and remove inside door 
handle cup (22635). 

Remove two screws retaining seat regulator control (14776) to inside 
door handle cup. 

To gain access to seat regulator control connector, remove the window 
regulator switch housing mounted in the arm rest. Refer to Seat Regulator 
Control Switch, Power�Six-Way, Removal and Installation as 
outlined. 

Disconnect seat regulator control connector and remove seat regulator 
control. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Recliner, Manual

 Bench, Split 

 Removal and Installation 

The front seat regulator requires no cleaning or maintenance. 

Remove spring clip and front seat back adjusting handle (61198). Retain 
the parts for installation. 

Detach J-retainer and arrow retainers at outboard right rear corner and 
J-retainer from cushion frame side. Pull back trim cover.

Remove push pins from recliner cover at rear and left off recliner 
cover. Also disengage lumbar tube (if equipped). (Power only: Disconnect 
electrical connector.)

Remove two front seat back regulator to front cushion frame retaining 
screws (on outboard side) and the pivot bolt on the inboard side. Remove front 
seat back assembly.

Detach J-retainers at bottom of front seat back assembly and pull up 
seat back cover.

Remove two screws retaining front seat regulator to front seat back 
frame (61018) and remove front seat regulator. 

 NOTE: Check front seat regulator for proper operation prior to positioning 
front seat back cover (64416) and front seat back (64810). 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten front seat back 
regulator retaining screws to 23-32 Nm (16-24 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Head Restraints

 Removal 

Unscrew front seat head rest guide rod retainers (610A18). 

Pull up on front seat back head restraint (611A08). Compress foam in 
area of front seat head rest guide rod sleeves (610A16). 

Remove front seat back head restraint positioning springs. Pull front 
seat back head restraint up and out. 

 Installation 

Slide front seat head rest guide rod retainers onto front seat back 
head restraint posts. 

Compress foam in front seat head rest guide rod sleeve area. Install 
positioning springs on front seat head rest guide rod sleeves. 

Insert front seat back head restraint posts (notches on posts facing 
rearward) into front seat head rest guide rod sleeves and push down to engage 
positioning spring. 

Tighten front seat head rest guide rod retainers onto front seat head 
rest guide rod sleeves. 

 NOTE: Front seat back head restraint must operate smoothly throughout its 
range of travel, must remain in any fixed position, and must not be freely 
removable from the seat back. If any of these conditions are not met, check 
for proper installation of positioning spring onto front seat head rest guide 
rod sleeve. 

Adjust front seat back head restraint by applying hand pressure, either 
up or down, to center area of front seat back head restraint.

ADJUSTMENTS

Latch, Seat Back

The front seat regulator is modular and does not require adjustments. 
However, proper lubrication of a hesitant front seat regulator is permitted 
using Multi-Purpose Grease D0AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESB-M1C93-A and ESR-M1C159-A. 

The only authorized service permitted on either front seat regulator 
is the following: 

Tightening of all retaining screws as outlined. 

Replacement (in entirety) of a damaged or non-functional front seat 
regulator. 

Removal of any foreign material, such as tie straps, pieces of foam and 
trim. 

If a front seat regulator or component is non-functional or damaged, 
the entire front seat regulator must be replaced.

Windshield Glass

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window Regulator Control Switch 

The window regulator control switches (14529) are located in door 
armrests.

A master window regulator control switch on the LH front door armrest 
can be used to activate any or all of the power windows.

Passenger window regulator control switches activate the power window 
for individual doors only.

Window, Heated Back

 NOTE: The radio antenna is integral to the window glass and is serviced with

The heated back window consists of:

the grid lines, which consist of two layers. The first is brown as

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Switch and Light, Heated Back Window 

The heated back window defroster system consists of the following 
components:

A heated back window switch and light (18C621) mounted on the 
instrument panel (04320). 

The heated back window switch and light has a push button spring-loaded 
to neutral position to turn the system on or off. A timer-controlled relay 
turns off after approximately 10 minutes of operation. If more time is needed, 
the heated back window switch and light can be reactivated for another 10 
minutes by pushing the button. Repeat as required. 

Pushing in the heated back window switch and light electrically closes 
the normally open contacts in the heated back window switch and light. The 
contacts provide battery positive voltage (B+) to the back window glass grids, 
indicator, heated outside rear view mirrors and trigger the timing circuit. 
The contact will remain closed until the timer turns it off, the heated back 
window switch and light is pushed or the ignition switch is turned to OFF. 

Power for the control timer comes from the accessory terminal of the 
ignition switch and is available when the ignition switch is in the RUN 
position. The circuit is protected by a fuse in the fuse junction panel. 

For individual wiring harness applications, refer to Section 18-01 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer's concern by operating the power windows/heated 
back window to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Front door power window regulator damaged.

Front window run damaged.

Front door window glass out of window run.

Front door window glass broken.

Circuits open/shorted.

Loose, corroded connectors.

Damaged window regulator control switch.

Damaged window regulator electric drive.

Fuse.

In-line circuit breaker.

Scratched grid.

If the inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily 
serviced, correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and 
Verification.

If the concern remains after the inspection, use the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester, 007-00500 or equivalent, connected to the data 
link connector (DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) 
and to execute Self Test Diagnostics for the driver door module as outlined in 
 Section 18-04 . If after performing Data Link Diagnostic Test, the New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester responds with module NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED, go 
to Pinpoint Test A . 

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, GO to Symptom Chart to continue diagnosis.

If diagnostic trouble code (DTCs) are retrieved, GO to Driver Door 
Module (DDM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index.

If the driver door module cannot be accessed by the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test A .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Switch Tests, Window 

 Master Switch�Town Car 

Testing the master window regulator control switch (14529) should be 
performed with the window regulator control switch removed from the vehicle. 
Use a self-powered test lamp or an ohmmeter such as Rotunda Digital 
Volt-Ohmmeter 014-00407 or equivalent. 

Clip one test lead probe on Pin 3, which is grounded. 

With all window regulator control switches in the NEUTRAL position, 
Pins 7 through 8 should have continuity to Pin 3. 

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position (toward front of vehicle when in installed position). Pins 5, 9, 
11 and 7 should lose continuity to Pin 3. 

Push all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position (toward rear of vehicle when in installed position). Pins 4, 8, 
10 and 6 should lose continuity to Pin 3. 

Remove the test lead from Pin 3 and connect it to Pin 2 (hot feed pin). 
With all window regulator control switches in the NEUTRAL position, only Pin 1 
should have continuity to Pin 2. 

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position. Pins 5, 9, 11 and 7 should have continuity to Pin 2. 

Pull all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position. Pins 4, 8, 10 and 6 should have continuity to Pin 2. 

Push the lock-out switch to its detent position. Pin 2 should not have 
continuity with any other pin. 

If any window regulator control switch does not test as stated, replace 
the complete window regulator control switch.

Testing the master window regulator control switch should be performed 
with the window regulator control switch removed from the vehicle. Use a 
self-powered test lamp or an ohmmeter. 

Clip one test lead probe on Pin 6 which is grounded. 

With all window regulator control switches in the NEUTRAL position, 
Pins 15 through 18 should have continuity to Pin 6.

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position (toward front of vehicle when in installed position). Pins 10, 
9, 15 and 16 should lose continuity to Pin 6.

Push all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position (toward rear of vehicle when in installed position). Pins 11, 
17, 16 and 18 should lose continuity to Pin 6. 

Remove the test lead from Pin 6 and connect it to Pin 5 (hot feed pin). 
With all window regulator control switches in the NEUTRAL position, only Pin 
20 should have continuity to Pin 5.

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position. Pins 16, 15, 9 and 10 should have continuity to Pin 6.

Pull all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position. Pins 18, 8, 8, and 18 should have continuity to Pin 6.

Push the lock-out switch to its detent position. Pin 6 should not have 
continuity with any other pin. 

If any window regulator control switch does not test as stated, replace 
the complete window regulator control switch.

 Single Switch 

 NOTE: Testing of the window regulator control switches should be 
performed with the window regulator control switches removed from the 
vehicle. Use a self-powered test lamp or Rotunda Digital Volt-Ohmmeter 014-00407 or equivalent.

With window regulator control switch in the NEUTRAL position, there 
should be continuity between terminals 1 and 2. 

With window regulator control switch pushed downward, there should be 
continuity between terminals 2, 4 and 5, and 1 and 3. Terminal 6 should not 
have continuity with any other terminal. 

With window regulator control switch pushed upward, there should be 
continuity between terminals 2, 3 and 5, and 4 and 6. Terminal 1 should not 
have continuity with any other terminal. 

If the window regulator control switch does not test as outlined, 
replace the window regulator control switch. 

 Heated Back Window Switch and Light 

Ground Pin 4 and connect a jumper wire between Pins 2 and 3. 

Apply power to Pin 2. The indicator should not light. 

Momentarily actuate the heated back window switch and light (18C621) to 
ON. The indicator should come on and stay on after the heated back window 
switch and light returns to the normal position. 

The indicator should go off under any one or more of the following 
conditions:

Heated back window switch and light is moved to OFF. 

Jumper wire between Pins 3 and 2 is removed. 

Approximately 10 minutes has elapsed. 

 Heated Back Window Grid Wire Test 

Using a strong lamp inside the vehicle, inspect the wire grid from the 
outside. A broken grid wire will appear as a brown spot. 

Run the engine at idle. Set the heated back window switch and light to 
ON. The indicator should come on. 

Working inside the vehicle with a 12-volt dc voltmeter such as Rotunda 
Digital Volt-Ohmmeter 014-00407 or equivalent, contact the broad red-brown 
strips on the rear window positive lead to battery side and negative lead to 
ground side. The meter should read 10-13 volts. A lower voltage reading 
indicates a loose heated back window ground wire (pigtail) connection at the 
heated back window ground wire attaching screw. 

Contact a good ground point with the negative lead of the meter. The 
voltage reading should not change. 

With the negative lead of the meter grounded, touch each grid line of 
the heated rear window at its midpoint with the positive lead. A reading of 
approximately 6 volts indicates that the line is good. A reading of zero volt 
indicates that the line is broken between the midpoint and the B+
 side of the grid line. A reading of 12 volts indicates that the circuit is 
broken between the midpoint of the grid line and ground.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Door Window Glass 

 Front 

 Removal 

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Loosen front door glass run front retainer retaining screw and position 
front door glass run front retainer (21572) forward. 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to pry out the rivets as damage to the front door window 
glass (21410) would result. 

 NOTE: Prior to removing the rivet center pins, it is necessary to place a 
suitable block support between the door outer panel and the front door window 
channel bracket (23288) to stabilize the front door window glass during rivet 
removal. 

Lower front door window glass to gain access to two front door window 
channel bracket rivets and remove the center pins from rivets using a drift 
punch. Using a 1/4-inch diameter drill, drill out remainder of rivets. 

Remove front door window glass. 

[FIGURE: N8853B.gif]

 Installation 

Insert front door window glass into front door (20124) between front 
door belt line outside weatherstrip (21452) and inner panel. 

Position front door window glass into door frame and lower front door 
window glass to align with front door window channel bracket. 

Install two 1/4-inch rivets using Rotunda Blind Fastener Installation 
Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent (use of 1/4-20 x 1-inch screw and washer 
assemblies and 1/4-inch-20 nut and washer assemblies is optional). Tighten to 
9-14 Nm (80-124 lb-in). Do not exceed maximum torque. 
Equivalent metric fasteners may also be used. 

Adjust Front Door Window Glass as outlined. 

Install front door trim shield and front door trim panel. Refer to 
 Section 01-05 . 

 Rear 

 Removal 

Remove rear door trim panel (27406) and watershield. Refer to Section 01-05 . 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to pry out the rivets as damage to the rear door window 
glass (25712) could result. Prior to removing rivet center pins, it is 
necessary to place a suitable block support between door outer panel and rear 
door window channel bracket to stabilize rear door window glass during rivet 
removal. 

Remove Rear Door Glass run 
front lower retainer (25796) as outlined. 

Lower rear door window glass to gain access to the two rear door window 
channel bracket retaining rivets and remove center pins from rivets using a 
drift punch. Using a 1/4-inch diameter drill, drill out the remainder of the 
rivets. 

Remove rear door window glass.

 Front Door Show, Rear Similar 

[FIGURE: N8852B.gif]

 Installation 

Insert rear door window glass into rear door (24631) between rear door 
glass outside weatherstrip (25596) and inner panel. 

Position rear door window glass into rear door frame and lower rear 
door window glass to align with rear door electric window regulator (27008). 

Install two 1/4-inch rivets using Rotunda Blind Fastener Installation 
Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent (use of 1/4-20 x 1 inch bolts is optional). 
Tighten to 9-14 Nm (80-124 lb-in). Do not exceed maximum 
torque. Equivalent metric fasteners may also be used. 

Install Rear Door Glass run front
lower retainer as outlined.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Glass 

 Removal 

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN. 

Remove windshield wiper arms and blades.

Remove inside rear view mirror (17700). Refer to Section 01-09 .

Remove visors and drop headliner near windshield opening down to avoid 
cutting headliner during windshield removal. Place a small block of suitable 
material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer. Removewindshield side 
garnish moulding (03598) as required.

Remove cowl vent screen (018A16).

Remove windshield rear view mirror. Refer to Section 01-09 .

Remove front door weatherstrip (20530) from vehicle. Refer to Section 01-03 .

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the instrument panel. 

Use Rotunda Knife With Offset Blade 107-R1511 Rotunda Interior Auto 
Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent to cut adhesive. Refer to 
manufacturer's instructions when using tool.

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove windshield and moulding assemblies from vehicle using suitable 
suction tool.

[FIGURE: N6948D.gif]

Trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 and 1.5 mm (0.04 and 
0.06 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed,surface 
should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign 
objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal if 
necessary. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry. 

If painted sheet metal has been exposed anywhere along the flange, use 
the supplied wool applicator and apply urethane metal primer WSB-M2G234-C to 
windshield pinch weld.

Install foam dam (with self-adhesive backing) around windshield glass 
opening at end of metal flange, and at uppermost side of seal area. 

Place windshield glass (03100) and moulding assembly on a low, stable 
work surface, inside up. 

If moulding is already on glass, proceed to Step 4.

If moulding needs to be installed, use the following procedure:

Align "V" notch in ceramic paint and windshield outside moulding 
(03144) at top center. Fully seat windshield outside moulding along the top 
edge of windshield glass then work along sides and bottom edges of the 
windshield glass. 

Clean windshield with non-alcohol-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Prep WSB-M5B280-C2 immediately after 
application because it flash dries. Prep application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane 
Glass Prep WSB-M5B280-C2 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides and 70 mm 
(2.75 inch) wide along bottom. Wipe off glass prep and repeat prep application.

Properly align windshield glass to body.

Place windshield glass into opening. Center it top and bottom, 
side-to-side. Adjust lower glass stops if necessary.

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four 
sides of both glass and window opening.

Remove windshield glass and moulding assemblies from vehicle and place 
it back on work table.

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Primer WSB-M2G314-B to make 
sure of uniform pigment mixing.

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 21 mm 
(0.8 inch) wipe along top and sides and 70 mm (2.75 inch) wide along bottom.

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

 NOTE: Apply new urethane on top of existing material on pinch weld.

Apply an even bead of urethane WSB-M2G316-B around entire sheet metal 
pinch weld next to windshield moulding retaining leg. The bead should be 
triangular in shape, 16 mm (0.625 inch) high and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base.

[FIGURE: N13342A.gif]

Install windshield assembly onto vehicle, taking care to align marks on 
glass to marks on body. This must be done before adhesive skins over.

Remove spacer and install headliner, windshield wiper arms, blades,cowl 
vent screen, visors and windshield side garnish moulding.

 CAUTION: Use only urethane for service of air and water leaks in urethane set 
windshield. 

 CAUTION: When replacing urethane installed glass parts, the vehicle should not 
be driven until the urethane has cured. At temperatures above 13°
 C (55° F) and relative humidities above 
50%, adequate cure time is typically 12 to 24 hours (less at higher 
temperatures and humidities). See detailed instructions provided by the 
urethane manufacturer. Inadequate or improper curing may adversely affect the 
retention of the windshield. 

Install inside rear view mirror. Refer to Section 01-09 .

Check installation for air and water leaks in urethane seal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Back Window Glass 

 Removal 

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASS AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. 

Disconnect rear window defroster and antenna wires if equipped.

Remove interior garnish mouldings and drop headliner near back window 
to avoid cutting headliner during back window removal. Place a small block of 
suitable material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer.

Remove panel (52018). Refer to Section 01-05 .

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the rear package tray cover panel. 

Use Rotunda Knife With Offset Blade 107-R1511 Rotunda Interior Auto 
Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent to cut adhesive. Refer to 
manufacturer's instructions when using tool.

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove back window glass and moulding assemblies from vehicle using 
suitable suction tool.

[FIGURE: N6948D.gif]

Trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 and 1.5 mm (0.04 and 
0.06 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed,surface 
should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign 
objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal if 
necessary. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry. 

If painted sheet metal has been exposed anywhere along the flange, use 
the supplied wool applicator and apply urethane metal primer WSB-M2G234-C to 
windshield pinch weld.

Install foam dam (with self-adhesive backing) around back window glass 
opening at end of metal flange, and at uppermost side of seal area.

Place back window glass (42006) on a low, stable work surface, inside 
up. 

If moulding is already on glass, proceed to Step 4.

If moulding needs to be installed, use the following procedure:

Align V-shaped notch in ceramic paint and moulding (42404) at the top 
and bottom center, fully seat moulding along top edge of back window glass, 
then along the two sides. 

Clean back window glass with ammonia-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Prep WSB-M5B280-C2 immediately after 
application because it flash dries. Prep application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane 
Glass Prep WSB-M5B280-C2 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides and 70 mm 
(2.75 inch) wide along bottom. Wipe off glass prep and repeat prep application.

Properly align back window glass to body.

Place back window glass into opening. Center it top and bottom, 
side-to-side. Adjust lower glass stops if necessary.

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four 
sides of both glass and window opening.

Remove back window glass and moulding assemblies from vehicle and place 
it back on work table.

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Primer WSB-M2G314-B to make 
sure of uniform pigment mixing.

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 21 mm 
(0.8 inch) wipe along top and sides and 70 mm (2.75 inch) wide along bottom.

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

 NOTE: Apply new urethane on top of existing material on pinch weld.

Apply an even bead of urethane WSB-M2G316-B around entire sheet metal 
pinch weld next to back window moulding retaining leg. The bead should be 
triangular in shape, 16 mm (0.625 inch) high and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base.

 Removal and Installation

 (9-18 lb-in).

Window Regulator Control Switch�Front Doors

 Town Car 

 Removal and Installation 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Gently pry up the front portion of the window regulator switch housing 
(14527). 

Unhook the rear edge of the window regulator switch housingand remove 
the window regulator switch housing from the armrest cavity. 

Remove the two screws retaining the connector to the window regulator 
switch housing. 

Carefully pry the window regulator control switch (14529) from the 
connector with a small screwdriver. Take care not to damage the elect rical 
contact pins. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. 

[FIGURE: N13271A.gif]

 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis

Remove screw and pry up gently on the window regulator switch housing 
starting at the front. 

Remove the four screws retaining the connector to the window regulator 
switch plate (14524) driver door. 

Remove screw from armrest. Gently pull window regulator control switch 
from door. Remove two screws retaining connector to window regulator control 
switch at passenger door.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Window Regulator Electric Drive

 Front Door�Town Car 

 Removal 

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Place window glass in full up position and secure with tape.

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect window regulator electric drive wires at multiple connector. 

Remove three 1/4 inch rivets retaining window regulator electric drive 
bracket to inner panel. 

Remove window regulator electric drive retaining screws using a No. 2 
Scrulox® bit and separate window regulator electric drive 
(23394) from front door power window regulator minus motor (23208). 

Working through access hole, remove window regulator electric drive 
bracket from inner panel and slide window regulator electric drive back to 
access hole in door to gain access to three window regulator electric drive 
retaining screws. 

Remove window regulator electric drive from inside front door (20124).

[FIGURE: N13279A.gif]

 Installation 

Position window regulator electric driveto front door power window 
regulator minus motor. Install three window regulator electric drive screws. 
Tighten to 4-5 Nm (35-53 lb-in). 

Reposition window regulator electric drive in door.

Install rivets retaining front door power window regulator minus motor 
to inner panel (1/4-20 x 1/2 inch screw and 1/4-20 nut and washer assemblies 
or equivalent metric fasteners may be used). 

Connect window regulator electric drive wiring connector. Connect 
battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove tape and check front door window glass (21410) operation. Install 
front door trim shield and front door trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 . 

 Front Door�Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 

 Removal 

Remove front door trim panel and front door trim shield. Refer to 
 Section 01-05 . 

Place window glass in full up position and secure with tape.

Disconnect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect window regulator electric drive wires at multiple connector. 

Remove three 1/4 inch rivets retaining window regulator electric drive 
bracket to inner panel.

Working through access hole, remove window regulator electric drive 
bracket from inner panel and slide window regulator electric drive back to 
access hole in door to gain access to three window regulator electric drive 
retaining screws.

Remove window regulator electric drive retaining screws using a Torx®
 Drive Bit Set D79P-2100-T or equivalent and separate 
window regulator electric drive from front door power window regulator minus 
motor. 

Remove window regulator electric drive from inside front door. 

[FIGURE: N13278A.gif]

 Installation 

Position window regulator electric drive to front door power window 
regulator minus motor. Install three window regulator electric drive screws. 
Tighten to 6 Nm (53 lb-in). 

Position window regulator electric drive on inner panel and install 
three rivets.

Connect window regulator electric drive wiring. 

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove tape from window glass and front door.

Check front door window glass operation. Install front door trim shield 
and front door trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 . 

 Window Regulator Electric Drive, Front Door�Crown 
Victoria, Grand Marquis 

[FIGURE: N8849C.gif]

 Rear Door 

 Removal 

Remove rear door trim panel (27406) and watershield. Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Disconnect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect window regulator electric drive wires at multiple connector. 

 NOTE: Use care not to enlarge sheet metal holes in the door inner panel.

Remove three 1/4-inch rivets attaching the window regulator electric 
drive bracket to inner panel. 

Working through access hole, remove window regulator electric drive 
bracket from inner panel and slide window regulator electric drive back to 
gain access to three window regulator electric drive retaining screws. 

Remove window regulator electric drive retaining screws using a Torx®
 Drive Bit Set D79P-2100-T or equivalent and separate 
window regulator electric drive from rear door electric window regulator 
(27008). 

Remove window regulator electric drive from rear door (24631). 

 Installation 

Position window regulator electric drive to rear door electric window 
regulator and window regulator electric drive mounting bracket. Install three 
window regulator electric drive screws. Tighten to 5-7 Nm 
(44-62 lb-in). 

Position window regulator electric drive mounting bracket to inner 
panel. Install three rivets (1/4-20 x 1/2 inch bolt and 1/4-20 nut and washer 
assemblies or equivalent metric fasteners may be used). 

Connect window regulator electric drive wiring. 

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove tape from window glass and rear door.

Check rear door window glass (25713) operation, install watershield and 
rear door trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 .

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass�Method I

 NOTE: There are 2 methods for repairing terminal separation from glass and/or 
grid breaks. Method I involves soldering the terminal to the glass and Method 
II uses an epoxy adhesive.

A single break or any breaks that total 25 mm (1 inch) in one grid 
cannot be serviced. The back window glass (42006) must be replaced. For breaks 
less than 25 mm (1 inch) long, use the following procedure: 

 NOTE: If the first layer of the heated back window glass grid (brown) is 
damaged or missing, it will be necessary to apply brown Acrylic Lacquer 
Touch-Up Paint AL81-5477-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M2P100-B on the glass prior to applying the Rear Window Defroster Repair 
D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A. 

Service inoperative grid wires on back window glassusing Rear Window 
Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESB-M4J58-A as follows. 

 Surface Preparation 

Bring vehicle inside and warm it to 16°C (60°
F) or above. 

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments, or abrasive window cleaners on 
the interior surface of the back window glass as this may cause damage to the 
grid lines. 

Clean the entire grid line service area with Ultra Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to 
remove all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important 
that the repair area be clean and dry. 

 Mixing 

The bottle of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A and touch-up paint (if needed) must be 
at room temperature. Shake bottle for at least one minute for thorough mixing. 
Shake frequently during use. 

 Application 

Mark location of break on the outside of the back window glass. 

Using cellulose tape, mask off the area directly above and below grid 
break. The break area should be at the center of the mask and tape gap must be 
no wider than the existing grid line. 

[FIGURE: K3787E.gif]

 NOTE: If the brown layer of the grid is not broken or missing, apply only 
the silver grid repair compound to the break. 

Apply the correct coating in several smooth continuous strokes 
(allowing three to five minutes drying time between coats) across the break 
area using the brush applicator in the cap. Extend the service coating at 
least 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) on both sides of the break area. 

If both brown and silver layers of the grid are broken or missing, 
apply a coating of the brown touch-up paint across the break area first. Two 
coats may be necessary to obtain the proper color. Allow the touch-up paint to 
dry then apply three coats of grid repair compound allowing three to five 
minutes drying time between coats. The coating of the grid repair compound 
should extend at least 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) on both sides of the break area. 

Allow to dry for five minutes then remove the mask. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage grid line with razor blade. Additional repairs 
may be necessary. 

After removing the mask, check the outside appearance of the grid 
repair compound. If the repair compound is visible above or below the grid, 
this excess should be removed. This can be done by placing a single-edge razor 
blade on the back window glass parallel to grid and scrape gently toward grid. 

 Curing 

The service coating will air-dry in approximately one minute and can be 
energized within three minutes. Optimum hardness and adhesion occurs after 
approximately 24 hours. At that time, the serviced area may be cleaned with a 
mild window cleaner.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass�Method II

 NOTE: There are two methods for repairing terminal separation from glass 
and/or grid breaks. Method I involves soldering the terminal to the glass and 
Method II uses an epoxy adhesive.

Use a rear window defroster service kit to repair pigtail connections, 
and grid line breaks.

The service kit is available from: 

Marketing East Company

10 Liberty Street

North Andover, Massachusetts 01845

Telephone: (508) 689-9565

Any break in the grid longer than 25 mm (1 inch) cannot be serviced. The 
back window glass (42006) must be replaced. For breaks less than 25 mm (1 
inch) long, use the following procedure:

 Surface Preparation 

The vehicle should be brought inside and warmed to 16°
C (60°F) or above.

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners on the 
interior surface of the back window glass as this may cause damage to the grid 
lines. 

Clean entire grid line repair area with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner 
E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to remove 
all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important that 
repair area be clean and dry.

 Application 

Mark location of break on outside of back window glass.

[FIGURE: N12581A.gif]

Place masking tape (provided in kit), over break in grid wire, aligning 
holes in masking tape with grid wire.

Prepare service kit two-part epoxy.

Check expiration date of package. If hardener has crystallized, place 
package in hot water until the hardener softens.

Remove plastic clamp from package separating resin and hardener.

Knead package until resin and hardener are thoroughly mixed.

Cut corner of package to open.

Apply two-part epoxy, with stick provided, to wire grid break through 
cut-out in masking tape.

[FIGURE: N12582A.gif]

Carefully remove masking tape from grid wire repair area.

 NOTE: Care should be taken while using heat gun around interior trim.

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, heat grid wire repair 
area for one to two minutes.

[FIGURE: N12583A.gif]

 NOTE: Heated back window is now operational. Two-part epoxy will thoroughly 
cure in 24 hours.

Start engine, turn heated back window switch and light (18C621) on, and 
leave on for five minutes. Inspect grid wire repair area.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Lead Window Terminal Service�Method I

 NOTE: There are two methods for repairing terminal separation from glass 
and/or grid breaks. Method I involves soldering the terminal to the glass and 
Method II uses an epoxy adhesive. Also, grid line repair procedures are 
different.

Allow the back window glass (42006) to warm up to room temperature for 
30-60 minutes. 

Clean the bus bar in the area to be serviced using fine steel wool (3/0 
to 4/0 grade). 

Restore the area where the bus bar terminal was originally attached by 
applying three coats of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A. Allow approximately 10 
minutes drying time between coats. 

Working as quickly as possible to avoid overheating the back window 
glass, tin the bus bar with solder in the area where the terminal will be 
reattached. 

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, preheat the back window 
glass in the solder area to 67°-83°C (120°
-150°F) just prior to soldering the 
terminal on. 

Position the terminal on the bus bar in the area that was tinned and 
hold it in place with an ice pick or screwdriver. 

[FIGURE: L2447F.gif]

 CAUTION: To avoid damaging the bus bar, remove the soldering gun or iron as soon 
as the solder flows. 

Apply soldering heat to the pad of the terminal until the solder flows. 

Start the vehicle. Turn the heated back window switch and light 
(18C621) ON and leave it on for five minutes. Inspect the terminal and apply 
Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4J58-A to the required area.

LUBRICATION

Window Regulator

The front door power window regulator minus motor (23208) should be 
well lubricated to provide ease of operation. The front door power window 
regulator minus motor should be lubricated whenever the front door glass top 
run (21596) or front door power window regulator minus motor is removed, or 
excessive effort is required to operate the windows. To lubricate a front door 
power window regulator minus motor, apply an even coating of Teflon®
 Lubricant D2AZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M1C111-A or equivalent to the window regulator arm rollers 
(23240), shafts and entire length of the window regulator equalizer arm 
brackets (23230).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cigar Lighter and Ash Receptacle

The cigar lighter knob and element (15052) has a low-resistance heating 
coil which operates much like the coil used in a portable heater.

When the cigar lighter knob and element is pushed completely into the 
cigar lighter socket and retainer (15055), the circuit is closed and current 
flows through the heating coil to the ground.

When sufficient heat is generated, the cigar lighter knob and element 
overcomes the spring pressure of the bi-metal retaining fingers and is released.

 NOTE: Service procedures for cigar lighter knob and element (for Town Car) 
are found in Section 01-05 .

Ash receptacles (30702) and cigar lighter knob and elements are located 
in the center of the instrument panel (04320) and in the rear armrests.

SERVICE PRECAUTIONS

Live Air Bags 

 WARNING: SAFE HANDLING OF AIR BAG MODULES REQUIRES FOLLOWING THE PROCEDURES 
DESCRIBED BELOW FOR BOTH LIVE AND DEPLOYED AIR BAGS. 

 ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR BAG 
VEHICLE, AND WHEN HANDLING AN AIR BAG. 

 WHEN CARRYING A LIVE AIR BAG, MAKE SURE THE BAG AND TRIM 
COVER ARE POINTED AWAY FROM YOUR BODY. IN THE UNLIKELY EVENT OF AN ACCIDENTAL 
DEPLOYMENT, THE BAG WILL THEN DEPLOY WITH MINIMAL CHANCE OF INJURY. 

 IN ADDITION, WHEN PLACING A LIVE AIR BAG ON A BENCH OR OTHER 
SURFACE, ALWAYS FACE THE BAG AND TRIM COVER UP, AWAY FROM THE SURFACE. THIS 
WILL REDUCE THE MOTION OF THE MODULE IF IT IS ACCIDENTALLY DEPLOYED.

================================================================================
PAGE 2351
================================================================================
1996 Town Car/Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis

Section 01-12: Instrument Panel

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

SERVICE PRECAUTIONS

Deployed Air Bags 

 SAFETY PRECAUTIONS MUST ALSO BE OBSERVED WHEN HANDLING A 
DEPLOYED AIR BAG. 

 AFTER DEPLOYMENT, THE AIR BAG SURFACE MAY CONTAIN DEPOSITS OF 
SODIUM HYDROXIDE, A PRODUCT OF THE GAS GENERANT COMBUSTION THAT IS IRRITATING 
TO THE SKIN. 

 ALWAYS WEAR GLOVES AND SAFETY GLASSES WHEN HANDLING A DEPLOYED 
AIR BAG. 

 WASH YOUR HANDS WITH MILD SOAP AND WATER AFTERWARDS.

PARTS REPLACEMENT

Steering Column Tube

If the collision involved an air bag deployment, the steering column 
tube (3514) may have been loaded sufficiently to deform steering column 
bracket insulator (3682) or damage steering column tube wiring. An inspection 
should be made of the steering column tube structure and air bag sliding 
contact (14A664) wiring to ensure that any damaged components are replaced. 
Refer to Section 11-04 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Cluster Finish Panel 

 Crown Victoria 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove two screws retaining instrument panel finish panel (044D70). 
Remove instrument panel finish panel. 

Disconnect time only clock and heated rear defrost switch.

Remove RH instrument panel upper moulding (04268) and LH instrument 
panel moulding (04389) from instrument panel (04320) by pulling away from 
instrument panel and snapping out of retainers. 

Remove radio chassis (18806). Refer to Section 15-00 .

Remove eight screws retaining instrument panel finish panel to 
instrument panel. 

Pull instrument panel finish panel away from instrument panel while 
unsnapping RH and LH upper corner retainers and disconnect wiring. Remove 
instrument panel finish panel from vehicle. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

Verify air bag warning indicator operation. Refer to Section 01-20B . 

 Town Car, Grand Marquis 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove two screws retaining instrument panel finish panel. Remove 
instrument panel finish panel. 

Disconnect time only clock and heated rear defrost switch.

Remove RH instrument panel upper moulding and LH instrument panel 
moulding from instrument panel by pulling away from instrument panel and 
snapping out of retainers. 

Remove radio chassis. Refer to Section 15-00 .

On Town Car, remove 13 screws (six at top and seven at bottom) retaining 
instrument panel finish panel to instrument panel. On Grand Marquis, remove 
eight screws (four top and four bottom) retaining instrument panel finish 
panel to instrument panel. 

Remove air bag. Refer to Section 01-20B . 

Pull instrument panel finish panel away from instrument panel and 
disconnect wiring. Remove instrument panel finish panel from vehicle. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. 

Verify air bag warning indicator operation. Refer to Section 01-20B .

Section 01-14A: Handles, Locks, Latches and Mechanisms

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Door Locks

 Power 

The power door lock system consists of:

door latch remote control and links.

door latches.

door latch control rod knobs (21850).

door handle (22404).

door latch actuating rods.

door lock cylinders (21985).

front door latch control cylinder rods (22134).

door latch striker plate (22008).

front doors (20124).

rear doors (24630).

door lock switches (14028) in the front door trim panel (23942).

power door lock actuator (218A42) inside each front door.

driver door module.

circuit wiring and circuit protection.

In the NEUTRAL position, each terminal of the power door lock actuator 
is connected to ground through the driver door module. Power is supplied to 
the system through fuse junction panel circuit breaker and Circuit 517 
(BK/W)(Town Car), Circuit 171(BK/W)(Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis). The 
circuit breaker is hot at all times.

When the raised portion of either door lock switch rocker knob (marked 
L) is pressed:

power flows through the door lock switch to the driver door module, 
which powers the lock terminal on the power door lock actuator.

all doors lock.

When the depressed portion of either door lock switch rocker knob 
(marked U) is pressed:

power flows through the door lock switch to the driver door module 
which powers the unlock terminal on the power door lock actuator.

all doors unlock.

1996 Town Car/Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis

Section 01-14A: Handles, Locks, Latches and Mechanisms

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lock, Child Safety 

The child safety lock, when activated, prevents the rear door (24630) 
from being opened from inside the vehicle regardless of the position of the 
rear door latch push button rod (26460). 

The child safety lock has been designed into the rear door latch 
(26412). 

A decal on the rear door lock face shows the location of the lever. 

The lever is manually moved up to lock and down to unlock the child 
safety lock system. 

Once the child safety lock lever is put into the locked position and the 
rear door is closed, the rear door can only be opened from outside the vehicle. 

The child safety lock does not lock the rear door from the outside. 

It is still necessary to push the door lock knob down or press the door 
lock switch (14028) to lock the rear door from outside.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Luggage Compartment Remote Control Lock Switch

The luggage compartment remote control lock switch (19C542) is mounted 
on the driver side front door trim panel (23942). 

It inputs a signal to driver door module which actuates a solenoid 
integral to the luggage compartment door latch (43200).

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer's concern by operating the power door locks to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Door alignment.

Latch damage.

Latch binding.

Failed circuit breaker

Corroded connectors.

Loose connections.

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data 
link connector (DLC) to retrieve diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to 
execute Self Test Diagnostics for the driver door module and lighting control 
module as outlined in Section 18-04 .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go the Driver Door 
Module (DDM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) Index to continue diagnostics.

If the driver door module cannot be accessed by the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent, go to Pinpoint 
Test A (Town Car) or Pinpoint Test B 
(Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis). If the lighting control module cannot be 
accessed, go to Pinpoint Test C .

 Driver Door Module (DDM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCS) Index

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Switch Door Lock, Master/Passenger 

 Town Car 

Use a self-powered voltmeter or an ohmmeter to test the door lock 
switch (14028). 

With the door lock switch in the NEUTRAL position, there should be no 
continuity between terminal 2 and terminals 3 and 4. 

When the raised portion of the door lock switch rocker knob (marked L) 
is pushed, there should be continuity between terminals 3 and 2 on LH lock 
switch, and terminals 3 and 4 on RH lock switch. 

When the depressed portion of the door lock switch rocker knob (marked 
U) is pushed, there should be continuity between terminals 3 and 4 on LH lock 
switch and terminals 3 and 2 on RH lock switch. 

If the door lock switch does not test as stated, replace the entire 
door lock switch housing and wiring assembly. 

[FIGURE: N13181A.gif]

[FIGURE: N13182A.gif]

 Master Switch/RH Front Switch 

 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 

Testing should be performed with the window regulator control switch 
(14529) removed from the vehicle. Use a self-powered voltmeter or an ohmmeter. 

Clip one test lead probe on Terminal 2 (ground). 

With all door lock switches in the NEUTRAL position, no terminal should 
have continuity to Terminal 2.

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position (toward rear of vehicle when in installed position). Terminals 
8, 9, 15 and 16 should lose continuity to Terminal 2. 

Push all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position (toward rear of vehicle when in installed position). Terminals 
10, 11, 17 and 18 should lose continuity to Terminal 2. 

Remove the test lead from Terminal 2 and connect it to Terminal 19 
(power).

With lockout window regulator control switch in neutral position, there 
should be continuity between Terminals 20 and 19. With lockout window 
regulator control switch in unlock position, no continuity should be between 
Terminals 20 and 19. 

Push all four window regulator control switches forward and hold in 
that position. Terminals 8, 9, 17 and 16 should have continuity to Terminal 
19. 

Pull all four window regulator control switches rearward and hold in 
that position. Terminals 10, 11, 17 and 18 should have continuity to Terminal 
19. 

Push the lockout window regulator control switch to its detent 
position. Terminal 19 should not have continuity with any other terminal. 

Remove test lead from Terminal 19 and connect to Terminal 5. 

Activate door lock switch to unlock. Continuity should show between 
Terminals 7 and 5. 

Activate door lock switch to lock. Continuity should show between 
Terminals 5 and 3. 

If any switch does not test as stated, replace the complete switch 
assembly. 

 Master Switch 

[FIGURE: N10393B.gif]

 RH Front Switch 

[FIGURE: N10394C.gif]

 Actuator, Power Door Lock 

Apply 12 volts directly to the power door lock actuator terminals 
(reverse polarity for opposite direction). The power door lock actuator rod 
should finish its travel in less than one second.

Using Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or equivalent, the power 
door lock actuator current draw (stall test) should not exceed 6 amps. Reverse 
the polarity to the connector and retest.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Latch, Door

 Front 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and watershield. Refer to Section 01-05 .

Check all connections on front door latch (21812) and front door latch 
remote control and link (21818) and service if necessary.

Remove one screw retaining front door latch remote control and link to 
front door (20124) and front door latch remote control and link retaining 
clip. Remove front door latch remote control and link.

Remove clip retaining front door latch control cylinder rod (22134) to 
door lock cylinder (21985).

Remove clip from power door lock actuator (218A42).

Remove clip retaining door latch control rod knob (21850) to front door 
latch.

Remove clip retaining front door latch actuating rod (22152) to front 
door latch.

Remove three screws retaining front door latch to front door.

Remove front door latch (with front door latch control cylinder rod) 
and anti-theft shield from front door cavity.

Transfer bushings and retaining clips along with front door latch 
control cylinder rod and anti-theft shield to new front door latch.

To install, reverse Removal procedure and tighten front door latch 
retaining bolts to 4-8 Nm (35-70 lb-in). Tighten front door 
latch remote control and link retaining screws to 1-2 Nm 
(9-17 lb-in).

 Fuel Filler 

 Removal and Installation 

Open the luggage compartment, push the override handle through the slit 
in the luggage compartment trim and pull back the trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 .

Open the fuel filler door and remove two screws retaining the fuel 
filler door latch (28610) to the housing assembly.

ADJUSTMENTS

Striker, Door Latch

 NOTE: This procedure applies to front and rear. 

 NOTE: Do not try to correct a poor door alignment with door latch striker 
plate (22008) adjustments.

Before adjusting door latch striker plate, open and close door to 
double-check door latch striker plate alignment.

 Drive Bit Set D79P-2100-T or equivalent. Move door latch 
striker plate up-or-down or from side-to-side as necessary. Tighten door latch 
striker plate retaining screws to 33-45 Nm (24-33 lb-ft).

Section 01-14A: Handles, Locks, Latches and Mechanisms

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Latch and Striker, Luggage Compartment Door 

The luggage compartment latch striker can be adjusted up and down and 
the luggage compartment door latch (43200) can be adjusted from side-to-side. 

Before adjusting the luggage compartment door latch, make sure that the 
luggage compartment door (40110) is properly aligned. 

Adjust the luggage compartment door latch as follows: 

Loosen the retaining screws. 

Move the luggage compartment door latch as required to enter the 
liftgate/luggage compartment latch striker (404A42) without deflecting the 
luggage compartment door sideways. 

Tighten the retaining screws to 9-14 Nm (7-10 lb-ft). 

Move the liftgate/luggage compartment latch striker up or down as 
necessary to provide proper luggage compartment door seal between the luggage 
compartment door and the lower back panel.

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Door Lock Control System, Electronic

The electronic door lock control system has three main components: 

The driver door module.

The five-button keyless entry keypad (14A626) on the driver door.

The four-button (hand-held) keyless entry remote transmitter (15K601). 

[FIGURE: N12339B.gif]

[FIGURE: N8498D.gif]

The driver door module will perform the following functions: 

unlock driver door

unlock all doors

unlock luggage compartment door (40110) 

lock all doors.

automatically lock all doors when all doors are closed, the ignition 
switch is in the RUN position, someone is seated in the driver seat, and the 
transmission is shifted into any forward or reverse gear. 

arm and disarm the anti-theft alarm control (19A366) (Town Car) 

provides a signal to the lighting control module which will:

turn on interior lamps (13776), keyless entry keypad and door lock 
cylinder illumination after any button on the keyless entry keypad is pushed 
or either front door handle (22404) is lifted 

turn on interior lamps, and door lock cylinder illumination when using 
the keyless entry remote transmitter. 

activate and deactivate personal security feature which sounds horn 
(13832) and flashes park lamps. 

The driver door module will also accept and store an alternate entry 
code. Either code will then operate the system.

================================================================================

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inputs and Outputs 

The electronic door lock control system receives signals from: 

transmission range (TR) sensor

ignition switch (11572) 

seat occupied switch

door lock switches (14028)

lighting control module (door ajar output)

keyless entry keypad (14A626)

keyless entry remote transmitters (15K601)

The system sends output signals to: 

keyless entry keypad illumination

power door lock actuators (218A42)

luggage compartment door lock solenoid (14030)

horn relay (14N089) 

lighting control module

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Entry Code 

The system's permanent entry code is located in four places: 

on the owner's warranty card. 

on a label on the inside of the luggage compartment door (40110). 

on an owner's code card. 

on the driver door module. 

[FIGURE: N6954B.gif]

The driver door module is programmed at the factory with a five-digit 
entry code. Replacement driver door modules include replacement labels and a 
new owner's code card.

1996 Town Car/Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Keyless Entry Keypad

To unlock the driver door, and disarm the anti-theft alarm control 
(19A366) (if equipped), enter the permanent factory code or enter the owner's 
alternate code. 

To unlock the passenger door(s), press the 3/4 button within five 
seconds of unlocking the driver door or luggage compartment. 

To unlock the luggage compartment door (40110), press the 5/6 button 
within five seconds of unlocking driver or passenger door(s). 

To turn on the courtesy lamps and light all illuminated components, 
lift either front door handle (22404) or press any button on the keyless entry 
keypad (14A626). 

To lock all doors, press the 7/8 and 9/0 buttons at the same time with 
all doors closed. (It is not necessary to enter the key code first.) This will 
turn off courtesy lamps and arm anti-theft alarm control (if equipped). 

To program a transmitter:

Each transmitter to be used with a vehicle must be programmed to the 
vehicle. Up to four transmitters can be programmed to a single vehicle. All 
transmitters must be programmed in the same session. 

Enter the five-digit permanent entry code into keyless entry keypad. 

Within five seconds, press 1/2 switch. 

Within five seconds, press any button on the first transmitter. The 
locks will cycle to confirm successful programming. 

Within five seconds, press any button on the second transmitter. 

Repeat Step 3 for each additional transmitter (up to four total). 

Press 7/8 and 9/0 together to end the programming session or wait more 
than 7.5 seconds. 

To program an alternate code: 

Enter the five digit permanent entry code into keyless entry keypad. 

Within five seconds of pressing last button of permanent code, press 
the 1/2 button and enter any alternate five digit code within five seconds of 
pressing 1/2 button. 

Enter a sixth digit as follows to indicate operator's memory seat 
setting to be recalled by alternate code:

9/0�no memory recall

1/2�memory seat position 1

3/4�memory seat position 2

5/6�memory seat position 3

After successful programming, the doors will signal by locking and then 
unlocking.

1996 Town Car/Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Autolock 

All doors will automatically lock after all the following steps are 
completed:

The autolock feature is activated. 

The driver seat is occupied. 

All doors are completely closed. 

The ignition switch is in the RUN position. 

The gearshift lever is moved into any forward or reverse gear.

After initial lock, all doors automatically relock when any door is 
opened and then closed except if driver seat is empty or ignition switch is 
OFF. 

To activate the autolock feature: 

Enter the five-digit permanent entry code into keyless entry keypad 
(14A626). 

Press and hold the 7/8 button on the keyless entry keypad within five 
seconds of entering the code. 

Press and then release the 3/4 button within five seconds of pressing 
and holding the 7/8 button. 

Release the 7/8 button on keyless entry keypad within five seconds of 
releasing the 3/4 button. 

To deactivate the autolock, repeat the above sequence.

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Transmitter, Keyless Entry Remote

 NOTE: The electronic door lock control system will not function when the 
ignition switch is in the RUN or ACC position.

The electronic door lock control system includes two four-button 
(hand-held) keyless entry remote transmitters (15K601). Up to four 
transmitters can be programmed to a single vehicle. For programming procedure, 
refer to Keyless Entry Keypad. Keyless entry remote transmitter are 
reprogrammable and all keyless entry remote transmitters for the vehicle must 
be programmed in the same session. When troubleshooting the system, one 
keyless entry remote transmitter is essential to perform tests. 

To unlock the driver front door, press the UNLOCK button on a keyless 
entry remote transmitter which is programmed once into the driver door module. 

Unlock will also disarm the anti-theft alarm control (19A366) (Town 
Car). 

To unlock both front doors, press the UNLOCK button on the keyless 
entry remote transmitter a second time within five seconds of the first 
unlock. 

If more than five seconds have elapsed since the first press of the 
UNLOCK button, pressing the UNLOCK button again will only unlock the driver 
front door. 

To unlock the luggage compartment door (40110), press the TRUNK button 
twice on the keyless entry remote transmitter. Two presses are required to 
prevent inadvertent luggage compartment door opening. 

To turn on interior lamps (13776) and door lock cylinder illumination, 
press any of the following keyless entry remote transmitter buttons-UNLOCK, 
TRUNK or PANIC. 

Security lighting will turn on exterior lamps at low ambient light 
levels (with Autolamps on) when the transmitter unlock button is depressed. 

To lock both doors and arm the anti-theft alarm control, (if equipped), 
press LOCK button once on the keyless entry remote transmitter. 

To confirm that both doors have locked, press LOCK button again within 
five seconds of the first press. This will sound the horn (13832) and lock 
both doors again. 

To activate the personal security alarm, press the PANIC button on the 
keyless entry remote transmitter. The horn will sound and park lamps will 
flash for a maximum of 2 minutes 47 seconds. 

To deactivate the personal security alarm, press the PANIC button again 
or turn the ignition switch to RUN. 

Each transmitter to be used used with a vehicle must be 
programmed to the vehicle. Up to four transmitters can be programmed 
to a single vehicle. All transmitters must be programmed in the same session.

To program a transmitter:

Enter the five-digit permanent code into keyless entry keypad. 

Within five seconds, press 1/2 switch.

Within five seconds, press any button on the first transmitter. 
The locks will cycle to confirm sucessful programming.

Within five seconds, press any button on the second transmitter.

Repeat Step 3 for each additional transmitter (up to four total).

Press 7/8 and 9/0 together to end the programming session or wait more than 7.5 seconds.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Security Mode Operation

The driver door module also controls the panic mode functions. 

Upon activation of the panic mode by pressing the keyless entry remote 
transmitter PANIC button, the driver door module sends a signal to activate 
the horn (13832) for approximately 2 minutes 45 seconds and parking lamp 
relays for three minutes. 

The driver door module cancels the alarm if the PANIC button is pressed 
again or if the ignition switch is turned to the RUN or START position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Memory Seat, Town Car Only

Remote keyless system may control the memory seat function. 

Refer to Section 01-10 . 

Press the keyless entry remote transmitter (15K601) UNLOCK button once. 
This will unlock the driver door and move the seat to its corresponding memory 
seat position, acting as if the memory seat button has been pressed. 

Each transmitter has a memory recall 1 or 2 (not both) designation and 
an enable switch. The switch must be in the ON position to activate memory 
recall.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the electronic door lock 
control system to duplicate the condition. 

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply: 

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Binding Latches

Open Fuses:

Town Car

Fuse junction panel Circuit Breaker 14 (20A) Fuse 8 (15A)

Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis

Power distribution box - Circuit Breaker 7 (20A)

Fuse junction panel Circuit Breaker 14 (20A) and Fuse 8 (15A)

Loose Connectors

Corroded Connectors

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data link connector 
(DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute 
Self Test Diagnostics for the driver door module and lighting control module 
as outlined in Section 18-04 . If after performing data link diagnostic test, 
the new generation star (NGS) tester responds with module no response/not 
equipped, go to Pinpoint Test A for 
driver door module or Pinpoint Test B 
for lighting control module. 

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, GO to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, GO to the Diagnostic 
Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index to continue diagnostics.

If the driver door module cannot be accessed by the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent, GO to Pinpoint 
Test A . If lighting control module cannot be accessed, GO to Pinpoint Test B 
.

Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS)®, 
001-00001 or equivalent, may also be used to diagnose this system.

Section 01-16: Wiper and Washer Systems

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wiper System, Windshield 

The windshield wiper system consists of the following components:

windshield wiper motor (17508) attached to the windshield wiper 
mounting arm and pivot shaft (17566).

a windshield wiper motor output arm (17A436) which connects the 
windshield wiper motor directly to the windshield wiper mounting arm and pivot 
shaft.

multi-function switch (13K359), which features a rotary wiper switch 
and a push-type washer actuator.

windshield wiper control module (17C476) located behind the instrument 
panel between the radio and steering column. 

RH windshield wiper pivot arm (17526)

LH windshield wiper pivot arm (17527)

two windshield wiper blades (17528)

 Off/Low/High Speed 

The two-speed, permanent magnet, three brush electric windshield wiper 
motor operates in the following manner:

A brush rigging permits selection of low or high speed.

When the multi-function switch is in LO position the common brush and 
the blue/orange wire brush are used and the windshield wiper motor operates at 
low speed. 

When the multi-function switch is in HI position the common brush and 
the white wire brush are used. Electric current bypasses a portion of the 
armature winding, causing the windshield wiper motor to run at high speed. 

When the multi-function switch is moved to the OFF position, the 
windshield wiper motor will continue at low speed until the multi-function 
switch outer contacts open. When the park switch contacts open, the windshield 
wiper motor stops in the park position.

The windshield wiper motor switch is inside the motor gearbox.

 Interval 

When the multi-function switch is in the interval (INT) position:

The windshield wipers make single wipes separated by pauses. 

The control knob on the end of the multi-function switch sets the 
length of the pauses (from approximately 1 to 17 seconds). 

The length of pause decreases as the knob is rotated away from OFF and 
increases as the knob is rotated toward OFF. 

While in the interval wiper mode, it is normal to hear a slight ticking 
sound at the beginning of each wipe/pause cycle. This sound is from the wiper 
control module's relay. 

 NOTE: When using interval wipers, the first wipe may not occur until after a 
pause of up to 17 seconds. 

[FIGURE: K13878C.gif]
