REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Electronic Instrument Cluster 

 NOTE: The electronics within the instrument cluster (10849) are NOT 
serviceable. For a confirmed electronic failure, return the entire assembly to 
the manufacturer (packaged carefully to avoid damage to the vacuum fluorescent 
displays and other electronic components). Instrument cluster should be 
disassembled only to service plastic defects (refer to service part diagram). 

Federal law requires that the odometer in any replacement 
speedometer/odometer must register the same mileage as that registered on the 
removed speedometer/odometer. Service replacement speedometer/odometers and 
odometer modules with the mileage preset to actual vehicle mileage are 
available through Ford Electronic Service Centers. In nearly all instances, 
the mileage continues to accumulate in the odometer memory even if the 
odometer does not display mileage. This mileage can usually be verified by the 
electronic service centers. Contact the service center for instructions to 
receive a replacement speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the mileage 
preset to actual mileage.

If the actual vehicle mileage cannot be verified, the service center 
will supply a speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the odometer 
display preset to zero ("0") miles and the service odometer segment ("s") 
illuminated in the vicinity of the odometer display. In addition, an odometer 
mileage sticker is supplied with the replacement odometer. This sticker must 
display the estimated vehicle mileage and is to be affixed to the driver door. 

 Removal and Installation 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Set parking brake. 

Unsnap left instrument panel moulding (04389) and right instrument 
panel moulding (04388) off instrument panel finish panel (044D70).

Pull center panel switches (if equipped) forward, disconnect electrical 
connectors and remove the center switches.

Remove 7 screws retaining instrument panel finish panel and pull 
instrument panel finish panel out. 

Move gearshift lever to low gear (1) position if required for easier 
access. 

Remove connectors from headlamp and dimmer controls.

Remove instrument panel finish panel carefully so as not to scratch the 
instrument cluster. 

Disconnect electrical connector from front of instrument cluster. 

Disconnect transmission range indicator from instrument cluster 
carefully. Bend bottom tab down and pull transmission range indicator assembly 
forward. 

Remove four screws retaining instrument cluster. Pull instrument 
cluster out and disconnect electrical connectors on rear of instrument cluster. 

Remove instrument cluster. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten the instrument panel 
finish panel retaining screws to 2.7-4.0 Nm (24-35 lb-in).

 Disassembly

Reverse Steps 1 through 7 of Electronic Instrument Cluster Removal 
procedure to assemble instrument panel.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Electronic Instrument Cluster 

The electronic instrument system is made up of two assemblies. These 
assemblies are:

electronic instrument cluster (10849).

message center control and message center switch module (10D996) 
assembly.

The electronic instrument cluster consists of one microcomputer-based 
module that processes sensor information and controls the three vacuum 
fluorescent displays. The displays include the speedometer/odometer, the 
electronic fuel and engine coolant temperature gauges, and the message center 
control assembly. The following warning indicators are not included in the 
electronic instrument cluster:

Anti-theft (if equipped)

Anti-lock

Brake

Hazard

These warning indicators are located in the indictor lamp module. Refer 
to Section 13-08B for more information. 

All other warning indicators are included in the electronic instrument 
cluster and include: 

LH Display Warnings: 

AIR BAG*

Charging System*

CHECK ENGINE*

Safety Belt*

Oil Pressure*

High Engine Coolant Temperature

LOW FUEL

Center Display Warnings: 

SPEED CONTROL

High Beams*

Left Turn Signal*

Right Turn Signal*

RH Display Warnings: 

CHECK AIR SUSPENSION

OVERDRIVE OFF

DOOR AJAR

TRUNK AJAR

LOW WASHER FLUID

TRUNK AJAR

*These warning indicators cannot be dimmed. 

The electronic instrument cluster is operational only when the ignition 
switch is in RUN. The electronic vacuum fluorescent displays are powered by a 
nonserviceable internal power supply. The only illumination bulb used, which 
is not serviceable, is for backlighting of the transmission range indicator. 
When the headlamps are turned on, the instrument cluster dims according to the 
interior lighting control paddle position (except those warnings indicated 
above, which do not dim). 

 Electronic Instrument Cluster 

[FIGURE: K22831A.gif]

 Electronic Instrument Cluster Display Prove Out 

The electronic instrument cluster display prove out operates in the 
following manner:

Each time the ignition switch is turned from OFF to RUN, the three 
electronic displays will prove out by momentarily lighting all of the segments 
and then momentarily turning all display segments off. 

After the prove out, the three displays return to normal operation. 

Prove-out mode indicates that all display segments are functioning 
properly. 

After initial prove-out period with ignition switch in RUN, these 
warning indicators are off with the ignition switch in RUN (warnings will be 
on if in RUN, engine OFF). 

When instrument cluster receives a signal from a sensor, the instrument 
cluster processes that signal and turns on the respective indicator. For 
example: 

If the AIR BAG indicator is on or flashing, the air bag diagnostic 
monitor (14B056) has detected a fault in the supplemental restraint system. 

It warns the driver by sending a signal to the instrument cluster. 

Consequently the instrument cluster turns on AIR BAG indicator. Refer 
to Section 01-20B .

There are three exceptions to prove out: 

The turn signal and high beam indicators will not light during prove 
out. 

In addition, the safety belt, CHECK ENGINE, AIR BAG, and oil pressure 
warning indicators will remain illuminated during the blank portion of prove 
out and then go blank at the beginning of, or shortly after, normal instrument 
cluster display.

The charging system warning proves out by lighting when the ignition 
switch is turned to RUN, before the engine is started.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Indication System

 Fuel Gauge 

The fuel gauge operates in the following manner:

Fuel level is displayed on a digital bar gauge using 8 bars top to 
bottom. 

Fuel remaining is displayed in the fuel/temperature gauge. 

For fuel levels greater than 70 liters (18 gal), the letter F (full) 
is displayed. 

For fuel levels less than 3 liters (1 gal), the letter E (empty) is 
displayed. 

Liter or gallon values are selected by the English/Metric (E/M) button, 
in the message center switch module (10D996), located immediately to the right 
of the instrument cluster (10849). 

The digital displays are based on a varying current flow from the fuel 
level sensor (9275). 

When the fuel level is low, fuel level sensor resistance is low. 

When the fuel level is high, fuel level sensor resistance is high. 

 Fuel Indication Systems 

[FIGURE: K24971A.gif]

The fuel pump symbol is always on except during: 

prove out sequence � on/off/on. 

low fuel level warning � the fuel pump (gas pump) symbol 
flashes when approximately one-eighth of a tank of fuel remains. 

 Diagnostic Bars 

Diagnostic bars perform the following functions: 

When only the top and bottom two bars appear on the fuel gauge, this 
indicates that the resistance of the fuel level sensor is above or below the 
operating resistance range (above 168 ohms or below 11 ohms). 

Either an open or short circuit is present (refer to Diagnosis and Testing ). 

"CO" for circuit open or "CS" for circuit short will be displayed if 
function is selected (refer to Diagnosis and Testing ). 

There is a built-in delay of approximately 30 seconds from the time the 
circuit open or short occurs until the diagnostic bars appear, and a 30-second 
delay for display to return in CO or CS condition is eliminated. This is to 
prevent momentary intermittent conditions or circuit noise from triggering the 
diagnostic bars.

 Low Fuel Level Warning 

A low fuel alert is given by a flashing fuel pump (gas pump) symbol 
when the fuel remaining is approximately one-eighth of the tank.

 Fuel Level Sensor 

The fuel level sensor, which is combined with the fuel pump (9350), 
operates in the following manner: 

The unit consists of a variable resistor controlled by the level of an 
attached float in the fuel tank (9002). 

When the fuel level is low, resistance in the fuel level sensor is low 
and number of lit bars is minimal (from EMPTY position). 

When the fuel level is high, the resistance in the fuel level sensor 
is high and number of lit bars is greater (from EMPTY position).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System, Engine 

 Coolant Temperature Gauge 

The engine coolant temperature gauge has the following features:

This gauge is identified by a thermometer symbol. 

H means high temperature.

C means low temperature.

NORM means normal temperature. 

This gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature based on an 
operating resistance range from the engine coolant temperature sensor (ECT 
sensor) (12A648) (13,000 ohms maximum to 200 ohms minimum, from low to high 
temperature, where resistances above 13,000 ohms indicate temperatures below 
the range of the gauge). 

The number of bars lit increases as the engine warms up (from the 
lowest bar into the normal operating region). 

It is acceptable under certain driving conditions, such as heavy 
traffic or stop-and-go driving in hot weather, for the bar to point to the top 
of the NORM region.

 Diagnostic Bars 

Diagnostic bars on this gauge indicate that the resistance of engine 
coolant temperature sensor is lower than the operating resistance range (less 
than 200 ohms). 

When the top two and bottom two bars appear on the engine coolant 
temperature gauge, a short circuit may be present (refer to Diagnosis and Testing ). 

When the bottom bar and the thermometer and TEMP displays appear, an 
open circuit may be present.

 High Coolant Temperature Warning 

When the engine coolant is overheating: 

the bars in the engine coolant temperature gauge rise above the normal 
range. 

the thermometer symbol flashes. 

a tone sounds every five seconds to alert the driver.

 Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor 

Engine coolant temperature sensor: 

is mounted into the engine intake manifold (9424). 

sends a signal sent to electronic instrument cluster which varies with 
the resistance of engine coolant temperature sensor relative to the engine 
coolant temperature.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

The oil pressure indication system consists of: 

oil pressure sensor (9278) on the engine. 

engine oil pressure warning indicator in the instrument cluster.

 Low Oil Pressure Warning 

If the oil pressure drops below the normal range, the ISO (Oil Can) 
symbol will light and a tone will sound to alert driver.

 Oil Pressure Sensor 

The oil pressure sensor is threaded into the cylinder block. The oil 
pressure sensor reacts to the pressure of the engine oil in the lube passage. 
It is normally closed with engine oil pressure and opens with low oil 
pressure.

 NOTE: The symbol KM/H signifies a metric speed display and the symbol MPH

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Odometer 

The odometer operates in the following manner: 

Displays either miles or kilometers by pressing the E/M button. 

Displays seven digits, with the last digit in tenths of a unit. 

The odometer range is limited by the instrument cluster memory space. 

The English units range from 000000.5 to 925691.9 miles. (The display 
will freeze at this value.) 

The metric range is from 000000.8 to 858993.4 km where the value will 
roll over to 000000.0 and continue accumulating up to 622113.6 km (the 
equivalent of 925691.9 total miles). 

If the mileage on the original odometer is unknown, the replacement 
odometer will show no mileage. Then the S symbol is always displayed when the 
electronic instrument cluster is turned on (except during the OFF portion of 
prove out). 

If the actual vehicle mileage can be verified, an authorized service 
center can program the replacement odometer to reflect actual mileage (without 
the S symbol). 

If a condition exists where the electronic instrument cluster (10849) 
cannot read a valid odometer memory from the non-volatile random access 
memory, the odometer will display the word ERROR.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Message Center Control Assembly Switch Module

The message center switch module (10D996) is located immediately to the 
right of the instrument cluster (10849). It consists of four buttons: 

SELECT ( )

E/M

RESET

[FIGURE: K24175A.gif]

The electronic instrument cluster receives a resistance signal 
corresponding to the button being pressed (17,600 ohms maximum range). A tone 
is sounded when a button is pressed.

 Select 

The SELECT buttons display any of the selectable message center 
functions: 

Distance to empty (DIST TO EMPTY).

Average fuel economy (AVG ECON).

Instantaneous fuel economy (INST ECON).

Trip distance A (TRIP A) and B (TRIP B).

Average speed (AVG SPEED). 

The highlighted box indicates the feature. The button can be pressed on 
the right (forward) or left (reverse) side to move the highlight box to the 
right or to the left menu selection. 

 E/M 

The E/M button displays the function in either English mode (MILES PER 
GAL, GAL, MILES) or metric mode (LTR/100 km, LTR, km). This affects both the 
electronic instrument cluster and electronic automatic temperature control 
system if equipped.

 Reset 

The RESET button resets the called up message center function as follows:

Trip distance reset to zero.

Average fuel economy is reset to the instantaneous fuel economy value.

Average speed is reset to instantaneous.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Message Center Displays

The message center displays contain the following: 

average speed (AVG SPEED). 

instantaneous fuel economy (INST ECON).

average fuel economy (AVG ECON).

distance to empty (DIST TO EMPTY).

trip distance (TRIP A, TRIP B).

The message center takes in signals from the following electronic 
engine controls: 

vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731) (speed/distance). 

fuel pump module. 

powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) (fuel flow). 

The message center performs continuous calculations of a signal or 
signals to supply the information for each message center function. 

 Instantaneous Fuel Economy 

The instantaneous fuel economy (INST ECON) display: 

computes its reading based on distance traveled (vehicle speed sensor 
signal) and fuel used (fuel flow signal from powertrain control module) 
information. 

may indicate 0 to 99 miles per gallon or 1 to 99 liters per 100 
kilometers. 

displays 0 miles per gallon or 99 liters/100 kilometers. 

cannot be reset. 

 Average Fuel Economy 

The average fuel economy (AVG ECON) display: 

Computes its reading from distance traveled (vehicle speed sensor 
signal) and fuel used (fuel flow signal from powertrain control module) 
information. 

Indicates the value calculated since the last reset. 

May be reset by pressing the RESET button while the average fuel 
economy feature is displayed. 

 Distance to Empty 

The distance to empty (DIST TO EMPTY) display: 

is based on a calculation using an average of the fuel economy over the 
last 850 km (500 miles) and the current fuel remaining to estimate the 
distance that can be driven with remaining fuel. This distance may increase or 
decrease depending on the most recent driving conditions. 

cannot be reset. 

For proper distance to empty function, the ignition switch must be 
turned to OFF when fuel is being added to the fuel tank (9002). 

When distance to empty drops to 80 km (50 miles), the fuel computer 
overrides the current displayed function, and flashes the DIST TO EMPTY value 
for five seconds. The display repeats this function at 40 and 16 km (25 and 10 
miles). 

 Trip Distance 

The trip distance feature:

displays the elapsed distance since the last reset and can be used as a 
trip odometer. 

can be reset to zero by pressing the RESET button while the trip 
distance feature is displayed. 

registers up to 999.9 and changes to 0.0 when 999.9 is exceeded. 

TRIP A and TRIP B operate independently.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators 

 CHECK ENGINE (MIL) 

The check engine (MIL) warning information is sent by the powertrain 
control module (PCM) (12A650) on the data connector link connector. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed. 

The indicator remains lit during prove-out sequence and possibly for a 
short time after. 

If a condition is detected, the indicator lights continuously. 

No tone is sounded. 

The indicator goes out when the condition is resolved. 

[FIGURE: K13906B.gif]

Refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual if the MIL remains lit or is 
intermittent.

 CHARGING SYSTEM 

Charge system warning (battery symbol) is displayed when there is a 
concern in the charging system. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed. 

The indicator remains lit during prove-out sequence and possibly for a 
short time after. 

If a condition is detected, the indicator lights continuously. 

No tone is sounded. 

It goes out when the concern is resolved. 

Refer to Section 14-00 for additional information.

 LOW OIL PRESSURE 

If the oil pressure drops below the normal range, the low oil pressure 
warning (oil can symbol) lights continuously. 

When the oil pressure returns to normal, the warning goes out.

 HIGH COOLANT TEMPERATURE 

When the engine coolant is overheating: 

The bars in the engine coolant temperature gauge rise above the normal 
range. 

The thermometer symbol flashes. 

A tone sounds every five seconds to alert the driver. 

 AIR SUSPENSION 

CHECK AIR SUSPENSION warning is displayed when there is a concern in 
the air suspension system or circuitry.

Warning will sound one tone and flash on and off for five seconds. 
Dimming will be overridden when flashing if less than discernible dimming 
level. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed while flashing. 

During prove out sequence, a one-second tone is sounded. 

CHECK AIR SUSPENSION warning flashes for five seconds, then remains lit. 

When concern goes away the warning stops. 

Refer to Section 04-05 for additional information.

 TRUNK AJAR 

This warning indicates that luggage compartment door (40110) is ajar or 
there is a concern in the luggage compartment door open warning lamp circuit. 

Warning will sound one tone and flash on and off for five seconds. 
Dimming will be overridden when flashing if less than discernible dimming 
level. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed while flashing. 

During prove out sequence, a one-second tone is sounded. 

TRUNK AJAR warning flashes for five seconds, then remains on. 

When luggage compartment door is closed or concern goes away, the 
warning stops. 

 DOOR AJAR 

This warning indicates that a front or rear door is ajar or there is a 
concern in the door open warning lamp circuit. 

Warning will sound one tone and flash on and off for five seconds. 
Dimming will be overridden when flashing if less than discernible dimming 
level. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed while flashing. 

During prove out sequence, a one-second tone is sounded. 

DOOR AJAR warning flashes for five seconds, then remains on. 

When the front or rear door is closed or concern goes away, the warning 
stops. 

 LOW WASHER FLUID 

Warning will sound one tone and flash LOW WASHER FLUID indicator on and 
off for five seconds. Dimming will be overridden when flashing if less than 
discernible dimming level. 

This indicator cannot be dimmed while flashing. 

During prove out sequence, a one-second tone is sounded. 

LOW WASHER FLUID warning is present when windshield washer fluid level 
is below specified level or there is a concern in the windshield washer 
reservoir fluid level sensor. 

LOW WASHER FLUID warning flashes for five seconds, then remains on. 

When the windshield washer fluid level is raised above specified level 
or the concern goes away, the warning stops. 

Refer to Section 01-16 for additional information. 

 SAFETY BELT 

Safety belt warning operates as follows:

If driver safety belt is not fastened with ignition switch in RUN, the 
SAFETY BELT warning will illuminate steadily for approximately one minute. 

The safety belt warning chime in the lighting control module will also 
sound for approximately 6 (±2) seconds. 

If the driver fastens the safety belt while the safety belt warning is 
illuminated or lighting control module safety belt warning chime sounds, they 
will turn off immediately. 

Refer to Section 01-20A . 

 AIR BAG 

AIR BAG warning is displayed when there is a concern in the air bag 
system. Refer to Section 01-20B .

 HIGH BEAM 

This indicator will be displayed when the high-beam headlamps (13008) 
are on. 

 LH/RH Turn 

These indicators will be flashing when activated by the multi-function 
switch (13K359). They also operate in a dual flashing mode as a hazard 
indicator in tandem with the electronic instrument cluster if ignition switch 
is in RUN. If ignition switch is in OFF, the electronic instrument cluster is 
off and only the hazard indicators in the electronic instrument cluster flash. 

 OVERDRIVE OFF 

 NOTE: OVERDRIVE OFF warning will flash if there is a concern with the 
powertrain control module or electronic transmission (similar to CHECK 
ENGINE). Refer to Section 07-05 if this indicator is not operating properly. 

OVERDRIVE OFF indicator lights when the transmission is locked out of 
OVERDRIVE. This is done by pressing the transmission control switch button in 
the end of the gearshift lever.

 SPEED CONTROL 

SPEED CONTROL indicator lights when the speed control system is 
engaged. Refer to Section 10-03 for additional information. 

 LOW FUEL 

This indicator lamp (gas pump) comes on when the fuel gauge indicates 
approximately one-eighth of a tank. Ignition switch must be turned to RUN for 
this lamp to come on. 

 Transmission Range 

Transmission range indicator lamp is lit with ignition switch in RUN. A 
circle around the symbol indicates transmission range selected.

Inspection and Verification

signs of shorts, opens, bad connections or damage.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Electronic Instrument Cluster 

 NOTE: The electronics within the instrument cluster (10849) are NOT 
serviceable. For a confirmed electronic failure, return the entire assembly to 
the manufacturer (packaged carefully to avoid damage to the vacuum fluorescent 
displays and other electronic components). Instrument cluster should be 
disassembled only to service plastic defects (refer to service part diagram). 

Federal law requires that the odometer in any replacement 
speedometer/odometer must register the same mileage as that registered on the 
removed speedometer/odometer. Service replacement speedometer/odometers and 
odometer modules with the mileage preset to actual vehicle mileage are 
available through Ford Electronic Service Centers. In nearly all instances, 
the mileage continues to accumulate in the odometer memory even if the 
odometer does not display mileage. This mileage can usually be verified by the 
electronic service centers. Contact the service center for instructions to 
receive a replacement speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the mileage 
preset to actual mileage.

If the actual vehicle mileage cannot be verified, the service center 
will supply a speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the odometer 
display preset to zero ("0") miles and the service odometer segment ("s") 
illuminated in the vicinity of the odometer display. In addition, an odometer 
mileage sticker is supplied with the replacement odometer. This sticker must 
display the estimated vehicle mileage and is to be affixed to the driver door. 

 Removal and Installation 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 . Set 
parking brake. 

Unsnap left instrument panel moulding (04389) and right instrument 
panel moulding (04388) off instrument panel finish panel (044D70).

Pull center panel switches (if equipped) forward, disconnect electrical 
connectors and remove the center switches.

Remove instrument panel steering column cover (04459).

Remove four nuts retaining the steering column and lower the steering 
column.

Remove knob from headlamp switch (11654). 

Remove 13 screws retaining instrument panel finish panel and pull 
instrument panel finish panel out. 

Move gearshift lever to low gear (1) position if required for easier 
access. 

Disconnect electrical connectors from message center switch module 
(10D996).

Remove instrument panel finish panel carefully so not to scratch the 
instrument cluster lens. 

Disconnect electrical connector from front of instrument cluster. 

Disconnect transmission range selector indicator from instrument 
cluster by carefully bending bottom tab down and pulling transmission control 
range indicator assembly forward. 

Remove four screws retaining instrument cluster. Pull instrument 
cluster out and disconnect electrical connectors on rear of instrument cluster. 

Remove instrument cluster. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten the instrument panel 
finish panel retaining screws to 2.7-4.0 Nm (24-35 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Install instrument panel by reversing Steps 1 through 9 of Electronic 
Instrument Cluster Removal procedure.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Transmission Range Indicator

 Disassembly 

Disassemble instrument panel by performing Steps 1 through 9 of 
Electronic Instrument Cluster Removal procedure. 

Disconnect transmission range indicator from instrument cluster (10849) 
by carefully bending bottom tab down and pulling transmission control range 
indicator forward. 

Remove screw retaining control selector bracket and cable (7E363) to 
steering column. 

Disconnect cable loop from gearshift lever pin (7W441) on the 
transmission selector lever arm and support (7302) of steering column and 
remove transmission range indicator. 

 Assembly 

Reverse Steps 2, 3 and 4 of Disassembly procedure. 

Place gearshift lever in OVERDRIVE ((D)) position. 

Adjust cable tension wheel at steering column until red indicator flag 
is centered between the calibration dots below the (D). 

Move gearshift lever through all positions and check that the flag 
completely covers each graphic with no overlap into adjoining graphics. 
Covering the calibration dots in the NEUTRAL or DRIVE (N or (D)
) positions is acceptable. 

Reverse Steps 1 through 7 of Electronic Instrument Cluster Removal 
procedure to assemble instrument panel.

 Printed Circuit 

The instrument cluster printed circuit (10K843):

supplies current to the instrument panel lamps and warning indicators.

is made of copper foil which is bonded to the polyester-base film 
(usually referred to as Mylar).

is mounted to the instrument cluster housing and, due to its location, 
cannot be easily inspected and/or tested in the vehicle.

is vulnerable to damage when a probe is used for in-vehicle testing 
because the probe can pierce the printed circuit or, in some cases, burn the 
copper conductors.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System

The fuel level indication system consists of the following components:

fuel pump (9350) (located in fuel tank (9002))

anti-slosh module with low fuel warning (located on the back of 
instrument cluster (10849))

fuel gauge (9305) (located in instrument cluster)

necessary circuitry

 Fuel Gauge 

The magnetic fuel gauge has the following features:

The coils form a magnetic field which varies in direction according to 
the variable resistance of the fuel pump connected between two of them.

A primary magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to 
align to this primary field, resulting in pointer position.

The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a metal housing which has two 
holes for dial mounting.

The fuel pump changes resistance according to the level of fuel in the 
fuel tank.

 CAUTION: Do not remove magnetic gauge pointers; the gauge cannot be recalibrated. 
The pointer position varies proportionately to the current flow. 
There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for this gauge.

 Low Fuel Level Warning 

When the fuel level falls to approximately 1/16 of a tank, the low fuel 
indicator will illuminate.

The anti-slosh module with low fuel warning (low fuel warning switch):

is designed to reduce fuel gauge needle fluctuation caused by fuel 
motion in the fuel tank.

provides a low fuel warning when fuel gauge reads approximately 1/16 
full.

 Typical Installation Shown 

[FIGURE: K16221E.gif]

 Fuel Pump Module 

The fuel pump module consists of the following features:

A variable resistor is controlled by the level of an attached float in 
the fuel tank.

When fuel level is low, resistance in the fuel pump is low and movement 
of the gauge indicator pointer is minimal (from the EMPTY position).

When fuel level is high, the resistance in the fuel pump is high and 
movement of the gauge pointer (from the EMPTY position) is greater.

Section 13-01C: Instrument Cluster � Conventional

1996 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System, Engine 

The engine coolant temperature indication system is a magnetic type 
system that consists of:

Engine coolant temperature gauge (located in instrument cluster (10849)).

Engine coolant temperature sensor (ECT sensor) (12A648) (located in 
intake manifold (9424)).

Necessary circuitry.

 Engine Coolant Temperature Gauge 

The instrument cluster temperature gauge has the following features: 

It consists of three primary coils of wire called the bobbin, one coil 
is wound at a 90 degree angle to the other two. 

When power is applied, correct flowing through the bobbin and sending 
unit forms a magnetic field which varies in strength according to the variable 
resistance of the engine coolant temperature sensor. 

A primary magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to 
align at this primary field, resulting in pointer position. 

The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a metal housing which has two 
holes for dial mounting. 

The gauge pointer remains in position when the ignition switch is 
turned to OFF.

The gauge pointer moves to the correct position whenever the ignition 
switch is turned to RUN.

An instrument voltage regulator as used on previous models, is not used.

The engine coolant temperature gauge is located in the lower RH portion 
of the instrument cluster. 

 Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor 

The engine coolant temperature sensor is mounted into the engine intake 
manifold. The signal sent to engine coolant temperature gauge varies with the 
resistance of engine coolant temperature sensor. At cold coolant temperatures, 
the engine coolant temperature sensor resistance is high, and at high coolant 
temperatures the engine coolant temperature sensor resistance is low.

1996 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

Oil pressure indication system consists of:

oil pressure gauge

oil pressure sensor (9278) (located in the engine block)

necessary circuitry

 Oil Pressure Gauge 

The oil pressure gauge is a part of engine coolant temperature gauge 
(10883) assembly.

The magnetic gauge has the following features: 

It consists of three primary coils, one of which is wound at a 90 
degree angle to the other two. 

The coils form a magnetic field which varies in direction according to 
the variable resistance of the oil pressure sensor connected between two of 
them. 

A primary magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to 
align to this primary field, resulting in pointer position. 

The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a metal housing which has two 
holes for dial mounting. 

 CAUTION: Do not remove magnetic gauge pointers; the gauge cannot be recalibrated. 
There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for 
these gauges. 

 Oil Pressure Sensor 

The oil pressure sensor is threaded into the cylinder block. The oil 
pressure sensor reacts to the pressure of the engine oil in the lube passage. 
It is normally closed with engine oil pressure and opens with low oil pressure.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

Charge indication system consists of:

battery voltage gauge

generator voltage regulator

charging system warning indicator

necessary circuitry

 Battery Voltage Gauge 

Battery voltage gauge is a part of fuel gauge (9305) assembly.

The battery voltage gauge:

Indicates battery voltage when the ignition switch is in RUN (engine 
off).

Registers within the band during vehicle operation. 

Is not adjustable and should be replaced if inoperative.

 Charging System Warning 

A red charging system warning indicator is located in the instrument 
cluster (10849). This indicator glows when there is no generator output or 
when the generator voltage is excessively high. 

If the system is working normally, the following conditions will be 
present: 

With ignition switch OFF, charging system indicator symbol is off. 

With ignition switch in RUN (engine not running), charging system 
indicator is on. 

With ignition switch in RUN (engine running), charging system indicator 
is off.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speedometer 

The instrument cluster (10849) contains an electromechanical 
speedometer (17255).

The electromechanical speedometer receives speed information from the 
transmission-mounted vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731).

The circuit electronics are calibrated to drive the speedometer pointer 
to a location in proportion to the frequency of the input signal from vehicle 
speed sensor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Odometer

The odometer:

is integral to the speedometer (17255).

is driven by the vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731) input signal.

registers up to 999,999 and then resets to 000000.

 Odometer Replacement 

The mileage on replacement speedometer/odometers cannot be reset. If a 
replacement speedometer/odometer is installed, a label recording the vehicle's 
mileage and date at the time of the speedometer/odometer replacement must be 
attached to the driver door jamb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Brake System 

This warning is displayed when parking brake is not fully released or 
there is a leak in the hydraulic brake system. Refer to Section 06-00 for 
additional information.

 Anti-Lock Brakes 

ABS warning indicates that the anti-lock feature is disabled. The 
warning goes out when the concern is resolved. Refer to Section 06-09 .

 Check Engine (MIL) 

The CHECK ENGINE (MIL) warning information is sent by the powertrain 
control module (PCM) (12A650) on the data link connector (DLC).

[FIGURE: K13906B.gif]

Anytime a CHECK ENGINE (MIL) warning occurs, refer to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

 Charging System 

Charging system warning (battery symbol) is displayed when there is a 
concern in the charging system. The charging system warning (battery symbol) 
remains lit continuously while the concern is present. It goes out when the 
concern is resolved.

 Air Bag 

AIR BAG warning is displayed when there is a concern in the air bag 
system. Refer to Section 01-20B for additional information.

 Safety Belt 

If driver safety belt is not fastened with ignition switch turned to 
RUN, the safety belt warning will illuminate steadily for approximately one 
minute. The lighting control module chime will also sound for approximately 6 (±
2) seconds. If the driver fastens the safety belt while 
the safety belt warning is illuminated or lighting control module sounds they 
will turn off immediately. Refer to Section 01-20A .

 Low Fuel 

This light comes on when fuel gauge (9305) indicates approximately 1/16 
of a tank. Ignition switch must be turned to RUN for this light to come on. 

 Fuel Door 

The fuel fill door warning is displayed when the fuel fill door is 
open, and remains illuminated until the fuel fill door is closed. Ignition 
switch must be turned to RUN for this warning lamp to come on.

 Air Suspension System 

If equipped with optional computer-controlled air suspension, this 
indicator tells you if the air suspension system needs service, or if the air 
suspension switch (in the luggage compartment on the RH side) is OFF. Refer to 
 Section 04-05 .

Normally, the AIR SUSP indicator light will glow momentarily as you 
turn ignition switch to RUN.

 High Beam 

This indicator will be displayed when the high beam headlamps are on or 
when the high beam headlamps are flashed.

 LH/RH Turn 

These indicators flash when activated by the multi-function switch. 
They also operate in a dual flashing mode as a hazard indicator.

 Overdrive Off 

OD OFF indicator indicates that the transmission control switch on the 
gearshift lever has been pressed. When the light is on, the transmission will 
lock out OVERDRIVE, allowing operation in first through third gears only. 
Pressing the transmission control switch again will re-enable OVERDRIVE. The 
transmission will be in the O/D ON mode when the engine is started even if the 
O/D OFF mode was selected when the engine was last running. Refer to Section 07-05 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer's concern by operating the instrument cluster 
(10849) to duplicate the condition and by observing the indicators and gauges 
to determine if they are operating properly with the ignition switch:

In RUN with the engine OFF

In START before the ignition switch is released

In RUN with the engine running

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged fuel tank.

Engine coolant level.

Engine oil level.

Accessory drive belt.

Fuse 13 (15A).

Circuit wiring.

Switches or sensors.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the symptoms 
and go to the Symptom Chart.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Pinpoint Tests 

PINPOINT TEST A: INTEGRATED CIRCUIT DISPLAY(S) INOPERATIVE OR ERRATIC

 A1 CHECK CIRCUIT 640 (R/Y) 

Disconnect battery ground cable. 

Remove instrument cluster as outlined. 

Disconnect instrument cluster connectors C1 and C2.

Remove Fuse 13 (15A) from fuse junction panel. 

Using an ohmmeter, measure resistance between load side of Fuse 13 
(15A) and ground.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Cluster

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove LH instrument panel moulding (04389) and RH instrument panel 
moulding (04388). 

Remove the six retaining screws and remove the lower instrument panel 
steering column cover (04459) (Crown Victoria). Remove the five retaining 
screws and removeinstrument panel steering column cover (Grand Marquis). 

Remove screw fastening transmission range indicator column bracket to 
the steering column. Detach the cable loop from the pin and cane shift lever. 
Remove the column bracket from the column. 

Remove the four cluster retaining screws. 

Disconnect the cluster connectors from the instrument cluster back 
plate (10848) and remove the instrument cluster (10849). 

 Installation 

Position the instrument cluster to the instrument panel (04320). 
Connect cluster connector. Make sure the transmission range cable is routed 
properly (refer to Section 07-05 ). Install the four cluster retaining screws, 
tighten to 0.8-1.4 Nm (8-12 lb-in). 

Position the transmission range indicator column bracket to the 
steering column tube (3514) (locate pin in column slot) and adjust the 
transmission range indicator (7A110) as follows: 

Place the transmission selector lever arm and support (7302) on the 
steering column tube in the 1 position. 

Place the loop on the indicator cable assembly over the retainer pin on 
the shift lever. 

Secure cable bracket with screw. 

Shift the transmission selector lever arm and support into the (D)
 position. Adjust the thumb wheel on the steering column 
tube so the entire width of the pointer falls within the letter (D)
. 

When properly adjusted, the entire width of the pointer must fall 
within the width of the letter (D)and must touch the remaining 
letters or numerals when viewed parallel to the center line of the steering 
column tube from the driver's position. 

Position the lower steering column shroud (3530) and install the 
retaining screws. 

Connect battery ground cable. 

Check operation of the instruments.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Instrument Cluster Lenses

 CAUTION: The use of vinyl cleaners and similar other cleaning agents to clean 
the vehicle interior and/or indicator lamp lens has resulted in damage to the 
indicator lamp lens. The chemical content of these cleaning agents 
(O-dichlorobenzene, ethyl alcohol and/or Cellosolve), has produced fogging, 
spotting, stain, or splotches of the lenses, either through over-spray or 
direct use on the lenses. Therefore, extreme caution should be taken during 
interior cleanup to prevent over-spray of cleaning agents which contain the 
chemical contents mentioned from contacting the indicator lamp lens. 

The indicator lamp lens should be cleaned with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent commercial cleaning product meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M14P5-A, using a clean, soft, lint-free cloth. The Ford 
Glass Cleaner has been specially formulated for cleaning windows in automotive 
vehicles and is approved for use in cleaning the plastic indicator lamp lens. 
Read and carefully follow the directions on the container for best results.

 Printed Circuit 

The instrument cluster printed circuit (10K843):

supplies current to the instrument panel lamps and warning indicators.

is made of copper foil which is bonded to the polyester-base film 
(usually referred to as Mylar).

is mounted to the instrument cluster housing and, due to its location, 
cannot be easily inspected and/or tested in the vehicle.

is vulnerable to damage when a probe is used for in-vehicle testing 
because the probe can pierce the printed circuit or, in some cases, burn the 
copper conductors.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System � Natural Gas Vehicles

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY SYSTEM CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS OR REPLACE COMPONENTS 
WITH PARTS NOT ESPECIALLY DESIGNED FOR USE WITH NATURAL GAS. FORD MOTOR 
COMPANY HAS SPECIALLY DESIGNED THE MATERIALS, COMPONENTS AND SYSTEM 
CONFIGURATION FOR THE 4.6L (2V) CROWN VICTORIA NATURAL GAS (NG) VEHICLE, AND 
EACH PARTICULAR SYSTEM IS PRECISELY CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE 
USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS COULD PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION 
THAT COULD RESULT IN FIRE OR PERSONAL INJURY OR CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE. 

 WARNING: IT IS IMPORTANT THAT YOUR NATURAL GAS VEHICLE BE PROPERLY MAINTAINED BY 
FORD NATURAL GAS TRAINED PERSONNEL. IF A PROBLEM OCCURS, IT IS IMPORTANT THAT 
PROPERLY TRAINED PERSONNEL DIAGNOSE THE CAUSE. IF THE PROBLEM RELATES TO THE 
FUEL SYSTEM, PROPER PART REPLACEMENT IS IMPERATIVE TO KEEP YOUR VEHICLE 
OPERATING AT NORMAL PERFORMANCE. COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS COMPONENTS AND 
STANDARD FUEL COMPONENTS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. IF YOUR VEHICLE IS NOT 
SERVICED IN ACCORDANCE WITH NATURAL GAS FUELED VEHICLE PROCEDURES, DAMAGE MAY 
OCCUR AND YOUR WARRANTY MAY BE INVALIDATED. 

The natural gas vehicle fuel level indication system consists of the 
following components:

fuel tank pressure sensor

fuel indication module (FIM) 

fuel injection supply manifold temperature sensor

fuel tank temperature sensor

fuel gauge (9305) located in instrument cluster (10849)

low fuel warning switch (located on back of instrument cluster)

necessary circuitry

 Fuel Indication Module 

The fuel indication module:

houses the unique electronics required for natural gas systems.

is located in a marine housing in front of A/C condenser behind 
radiator grille.

The fuel indication module has the following functions:

Injector drivers: Accepts eight unmodified injector signals from the 
powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) and allows a peak-and-sustain current 
to flow through the injectors solenoids. No calculations are performed; the 
injector driver output is not determined by the fuel indication module.

Fuel gauge driver: Uses fuel temperature and fuel pressure inputs to 
calculate density of fuel and a lookup table to determine the output to the 
low fuel warning switch (through a combination of discrete resistors), which 
drives the fuel gauge located in the instrument cluster.

Power and ground supply:

Supplies power to instrument cluster components on Circuit 231 (BK/Y) 
when ignition switch is in RUN and START position. Ground for fuel gauge, 
slosh module and voltmeter is supplied on Circuit 570 (BK/W). Circuit 231 
(BK/Y) supplies power to the following components.

Instrument cluster connector C1:

fuel gauge

voltmeter

slosh module

low fuel lamp

malfunction indicator lamp

speedometer

Instrument cluster connector C2:

temperature gauge

oil pressure gauge 

ABS warning indicator 

OD OFF indicator 

brake warning indicator

air bag warning indicator

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

NGV Fuel Tank Pressure Sensor

The fuel tank pressure sensor:

is located in the upper tank vent box at upper fuel tank rack

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Coolant Temperature Indication System

The engine coolant temperature indication system is a magnetic type 
system that consists of:

engine coolant temperature gauge (located in instrument cluster (10849))

engine coolant temperature sensor (ECT sensor) (12A648) (located in 
intake manifold (9424))

necessary circuitry

 Engine Coolant Temperature Gauge 

The instrument cluster temperature gauge has the following features: 

It consists of three primary coils of wire called the bobbin, one coil 
is wound at a 90 degree angle to the other two. 

When power is applied, current flowing through the bobbin and sending 
unit forms a magnetic field which varies in strength according to the variable 
resistance of the engine coolant temperature sensor. 

A primary magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to 
align at this primary field, resulting in pointer position. 

The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a metal housing which has two 
holes for dial mounting. 

The gauge pointer remains in position when the ignition switch is 
turned to OFF.

The gauge pointer moves to the correct position whenever the ignition 
switch is turned to RUN.

An instrument voltage regulator as used on previous models, is not used.

The engine coolant temperature gauge is located in the lower RH portion 
of the instrument cluster. 

 Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor 

The engine coolant temperature sensor is mounted into the engine intake 
manifold. The signal sent to engine coolant temperature gauge (10883) varies 
with the resistance of engine coolant temperature sensor at cold coolant 
temperatures the engine coolant temperature sensor resistance is high, and at 
high coolant temperatures the engine coolant temperature sensor resistance is 
low.

================================================================================

Section 13-01D: Instrument Cluster � Natural Gas Vehicle

1996 Crown Victoria Natural Gas Vehicle Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

Oil pressure indication system consists of:

oil pressure gauge.

oil pressure sensor (9278) (located in the engine block).

necessary circuitry.

 Oil Pressure Gauge 

The oil pressure gauge is a part of engine coolant temperature gauge 
(10883) assembly.

The magnetic gauge has the following features: 

It consists of three primary coils, one of which is wound at a 90 
degree angle to the other two. 

The coils form a magnetic field which varies in direction according to 
the variable resistance of the oil pressure sensor connected between two of 
them. 

A primary magnet, to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to 
align to this primary field, resulting in pointer position. 

The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a metal housing which has two 
holes for dial mounting. 

 CAUTION: Do not remove magnetic gauge pointers; the gauge cannot be recalibrated. 
There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for 
these gauges. 

 Oil Pressure Sensor 

The oil pressure sensor is threaded into the cylinder block. The oil 
pressure sensor reacts to the pressure of the engine oil in the lube passage. 
It is normally closed with engine oil pressure and opens with low oil pressure.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

Charge indication system consists of:

battery voltage gauge

generator (GEN) (10300)

charging system warning indicator

necessary circuitry

 Battery Voltage Gauge 

Battery voltage gauge is a part of fuel gauge (9305) assembly.

The battery voltage gauge:

Indicates battery voltage when the ignition switch is in RUN (engine 
off).

Registers within the band during vehicle operation. 

Is not adjustable and should be replaced if inoperative.

 Charging System Warning 

A red charge system warning indicator is located in the instrument 
cluster (10849). This indicator glows when there is no generator output or 
when the generator voltage is excessively high. 

If the system is working normally, the following conditions will be 
present: 

With ignition switch OFF, battery charge indicator symbol is off. 

With ignition switch in RUN (engine not running), charge indicator 
(generator) is on. 

With ignition switch in RUN (engine running), charge indicator is off.

Speedometer 

The instrument cluster (10849) contains an electromechanical 
speedometer (17255).

The electromechanical speedometer receives speed information from the 
transmission-mounted vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731).

The circuit electronics are calibrated to drive the speedometer pointer 
to a location in proportion to the frequency of the input signal from vehicle 
speed sensor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Brake System 

This warning is displayed when parking brake is not fully released or 
there is a fluid leak in the braking system. Refer to Section 06-00 for 
additional information.

 Anti-Lock Brakes 

ABS warning indicates that the anti-lock feature is disabled. The 
warning goes out when the concern is resolved. Refer to Section 06-09 .

 Check Engine (MIL) 

The CHECK ENGINE (MIL) warning information is sent by the powertrain 
control module (PCM) (12A650).

[FIGURE: K13906B.gif]

Anytime a CHECK ENGINE (MIL) warning occurs, refer to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

 Charging System 

Charging system warning (battery symbol) is displayed when there is a 
concern in the charging system. The charge system warning (battery symbol) 
remains lit continuously while the concern is present. It goes out when the 
concern is resolved.

 Air Bag 

AIR BAG warning is displayed when there is a concern in the air bag 
system. Refer to Section 01-20B for additional information.

 Safety Belt 

If driver's safety belt is not fastened with ignition switch (11572) 
turned to RUN, the safety belt warning will illuminate steadily for 
approximately one minute. The lighting control module chime will also sound 
for approximately 6(±2) seconds. If the driver fastens the 
safety belt while the safety belt warning is illuminated or lighting control 
module sounds they will turn off immediately. Refer to Section 01-20A .

 Low Fuel 

This light comes on when fuel gauge (9305) indicates approximately 1/8 
of a tank. Ignition switch must be turned to RUN for this light to come on. 

 Fuel Door 

The fuel fill door warning is displayed when the fuel fill door is 
opened, and remains illuminated until the fuel fill door is closed. Ignition 
switch must be turned to RUN for this warning lamp to come on.

 Air Suspension System 

If equipped with optional computer-controlled air suspension, this 
light tells you if the air suspension system needs service, or if the air 
suspension switch (in the luggage compartment on the RH side) is OFF. Refer to 
 Section 04-05 .

Normally, the AIR SUSP indicator light will glow momentarily as you 
turn ignition switch to RUN.

 High Beam 

This indicator will be displayed when the high beam headlamps are on or 
when the high beam headlamps are flashed.

 LH/RH Turn 

These indicators flash when activated by the multi-function switch. 
They also operate in a dual flashing mode as a hazard indicator.

 Overdrive Off 

OD OFF indicator indicates that the transmission control switch (TCS) 
on the gearshift lever has been pressed. When the light is on, the 
transmission will lock out OVERDRIVE, allowing operation in first through 
third gears only. Pressing the TCS again will re-enable OVERDRIVE. The 
automatic transmission will be in the O/D ON mode when the engine is started 
even if the O/D OFF mode was selected when the engine was last running. Refer 
to Section 07-05 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify customer's concern by operating the instrument cluster (10849) 
to duplicate the condition and by observing the indicators and gauges to 
determine if they are operating properly with the ignition switch:

in RUN with the engine OFF.

in START before the ignition switch is released.

in RUN with the engine running.

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged fuel tank.

Engine coolant level.

Engine oil level.

Accessory drive belt.

Damaged fuse.

Circuit wiring.

Damaged switches or sensors.

If the inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data link connector 
(DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute 
Self Test Diagnostics for the fuel indication module (FIM) as outlined in 
 Section 18-04 . If after performing data link diagnostic tests, the New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester responds with fuel indication module, no 
response/not equipped, GO to Pinpoint Test A .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, GO to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, GO to the Fuel 
Indication Module (FIM) Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Index.

If the fuel indication module (FIM) cannot be accessed by the New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester, GO to Pinpoint Test A .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Diagnostic Instructions

The fuel indication module (FIM) monitors the components and circuitry 
required for fuel indication during normal operation. If an error or concern 
is detected, the fuel indication module (FIM) will store a diagnostic trouble 
code (DTC) in memory. DTCs are retrieved from the fuel indication module (FIM) 
using the Rotunda New Generation Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent. If 
a concern exists with an instrument cluster component that is not related to 
the fuel indication system, refer to the Symptom Chart 
to continue diagnostics, DO NOT perform fuel indication module (FIM) diagnostics. 

The components monitored by the fuel indication module (FIM) include:

fuel tank temperature sensor No. 1

fuel tank temperature sensor No. 2

fuel tank pressure sensor

fuel gauge

circuitry

Fuel gauge accuracy may be affected by certain conditions. These 
conditions will cause abnormal fuel gauge movement possibly causing 
unnecessary diagnostics. Make sure the following conditions do not exist 
before continuing with fuel indication system diagnostics:

Fast filling

After fast filling a vehicle the fuel gauge may drop as much as 1/8 of 
a tank. This is caused by the rapid expansion and compression of the fuel 
during fast fills. This is considered normal gauge movement.

Fast filling with the ignition switch in the RUN position may cause the 
fuel indication module (FIM) to store DTCs in error. With the ignition switch 
in the RUN position the fuel indication module (FIM) is monitoring the 
sensors. During fast fill situations the fuel temperature drops to extremely 
low temperatures, this may cause the fuel tank temperature sensors to drop 
below their operating temperature range, causing the fuel indication module to 
store a DTC. When fast filling is complete, the temperature sensor will return 
to normal operation after it reaches normal operating temperature range. 
However, the DTC will still be set in memory.

Fuel system leaks

Fuel system components which are leaking may cause inaccurate fuel 
gauge readings. Depending on the size of the leak, the fuel gauge may not be 
able to maintain an accurate reading if the fuel leak exceeds the slosh module 
and fuel indication modules ability to update the fuel gauge. This creates a 
possibility for the fuel gauge to be reading a fuel level but the fuel tanks 
are actually empty. Before diagnosing this type of concern make sure fuel 
system is not leaking. Refer to Section 10-01B .

Erratic instrument cluster operation

The fuel indication module (FIM) has an internal on-board diagnostic 
mode which is not used with New Generation Star (NGS) Tester diagnostic 
procedures. However, if the ignition switch is cycled from OFF to RUN four 
times and left in RUN position without the engine being started, the fuel 
indication module (FIM) will cause the instrument cluster to react 
erratically. Warning indicators will remain illuminated and the voltage and 
fuel gauge will move sporadically. If this concern exists, start engine. If 
the concern is still present, continue with fuel indication system diagnostics.

DTC B1219: FUEL TANK PRESSURE SENSOR CIRCUIT FAILURE

 B1219-1 CHECK PID TANKPR

Yes

No

GO to B1219-2 
 .

INSPECT connectors and pins for loose connections. RESTORE vehicle. 
RETEST system. If DTC B1219 is retrieved replace fuel indication module (FIM). 
RESTORE vehicle.

 B1219-2 CHECK CIRCUIT 791 (R/PK) FOR SHORT TO CIRCUIT 875 (BK/LB) 

Turn ignition switch to OFF.

Disconnect fuel indication module (FIM).

Install Rotunda Breakout Box 014-00322 or equivalent to fuel indication 
module harness connector, leave fuel indication module disconnected.

Using an ohmmeter, measure resistance between breakout box Pin 7 and 
Pin 46.

 Is resistance greater than 10K ohms?

Yes

No

GO to B1219-3 
 .

SERVICE Circuit 791 (R/PK) for short to Circuit 875 (BK/LB). RESTORE

 B1219-3 CHECK SIGNAL VOLTAGE AT FUEL TANK PRESSURE SENSOR 

Connect fuel indication module to breakout box and harness assembly.

Disconnect fuel tank pressure sensor connector.

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Using a voltmeter, measure voltage between Circuit 875 (BK/LB) and

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Cluster

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove LH instrument panel moulding (04389) and RH instrument panel 
moulding (04388). 

Remove the six retaining screws and remove the lower instrument panel 
steering column cover (04459). 

Remove screw fastening transmission range indicator column bracket to 
the steering column. Detach the cable loop from the pin and cane shift lever. 
Remove the column bracket from the column. 

Remove the four cluster retaining screws. 

Disconnect the cluster connectors from the instrument cluster back 
plate (10848) and remove the instrument cluster (10849). 

 Installation 

Position the instrument cluster to the instrument panel (04320). 
Connect cluster connector. Make sure the transmission range cable is routed 
properly (refer to Section 07-05 ). Install the four cluster retaining screws, 
tighten to 0.8-1.4 Nm (8-12 lb-in). 

Position the transmission range indicator column bracket to the 
steering column tube (3514) (locate pin in column slot) and adjust the 
transmission range indicator (7A110) as follows: 

Place the transmission selector lever arm and support (7302) on the 
steering column tube in the 1 position. 

Place the loop on the indicator cable assembly over the retainer pin on 
the shift lever. 

Secure cable bracket with screw. 

Shift the transmission selector lever arm and support into the (D)
 position. Adjust the thumb wheel on the steering column 
tube so the entire width of the pointer falls within the letter (D)
. 

When properly adjusted, the entire width of the pointer must fall 
within the width of the letter (D)and must touch the remaining 
letters or numerals when viewed parallel to the center line of the steering 
column tube from the driver's position. 

Position the lower instrument panel steering column cover and install 
the six retaining screws. 

Connect battery ground cable cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Check operation of the instruments.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Indication Module

 Removal and Installation 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY SYSTEM CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS OR REPLACE COMPONENTS 
WITH PARTS NOT ESPECIALLY DESIGNED FOR USE WITH NATURAL GAS. FOR MOTOR COMPANY 
HAS SPECIALLY DESIGNED THE MATERIALS, COMPONENTS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATION FOR 
THE 4.6L (2V) CROWN VICTORIA NATURAL GAS (NG) VEHICLE, AND EACH PARTICULAR 
SYSTEM IS PRECISELY CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT 
PARTS OR MATERIALS COULD PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT COULD RESULT 
IN FIRE OR PERSONAL INJURY OR CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE. 

 WARNING: IT IS IMPORTANT THAT YOUR NATURAL GAS VEHICLE BE PROPERLY MAINTAINED BY 
FORD NATURAL GAS TRAINED PERSONNEL. IF A PROBLEM OCCURS, IT IS IMPORTANT THAT 
PROPERLY TRAINED PERSONNEL DIAGNOSE THE CAUSE, IF THE PROBLEM RELATES TO THE 
FUEL SYSTEM, PROPER PART REPLACEMENT IS IMPERATIVE TO KEEP YOUR VEHICLE 
OPERATING AT NORMAL PERFORMANCE. COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS COMPONENTS AND 
STANDARD FUEL COMPONENTS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. IF YOUR VEHICLE IS NOT 
SERVICED IN ACCORDANCE WITH NATURAL GAS FUELED VEHICLE PROCEDURES, DAMAGE MAY 
OCCUR AND YOUR WARRANTY MAY BE INVALIDATED. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove eight push-pin retainers and remove upper radiator side cover.

Carefully unsnap and remove fuel indication module plastic shroud over 
harness connector and disconnect 60-pin connector from fuel indication module.

Remove two bracket bolts at upper end of bracket and pull hood latch to 
left and remove bracket assembly from vehicle.

 NOTE: Marine cover seal and mating bracket surface must be clean and dry to 
provide proper sealing. Use RTV silicone to repair any damaged seal or bracket 
surface if necessary.

Remove four cover screws using 5 mm socket, separate marine cover from 
bracket and remove fuel indication module.

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten marine cover to bracket 
retaining fasteners to 2-3 Nm (18-26 lb-in). Tighten fuel 
indication module assembly to radiator support retaining screws to 8-10 Nm
 (71-88 lb-in).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Instrument Cluster Lenses

 CAUTION: The use of vinyl cleaners and similar other cleaning agents to clean 
the vehicle interior and/or indicator lamp lens has resulted in damage to the 
indicator lamp lens. The chemical content of these cleaning agents 
(O-dichlorobenzene, ethyl alcohol and/or Cellosolve), has produced fogging, 
spotting, stain, or splotches of the lenses, either through over-spray or 
direct use on the lenses. Therefore, extreme caution should be taken during 
interior cleanup to prevent over-spray of cleaning agents which contain the 
chemical contents mentioned from contacting the indicator lamp lens. 

The indicator lamp lens should be cleaned with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent commercial cleaning product meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M14P5-A, using a clean, soft, lint-free cloth. The Ford 
Glass Cleaner has been specially formulated for cleaning windows in automotive 
vehicles and is approved for use in cleaning the plastic indicator lamp lens. 
Read and carefully follow the directions on the container for best results.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Horn Relay 

Remove relay (14N089), located in power distribution box.

lead to Terminal 87 of relay. Observe resistance.

Momentarily tap unconnected end of second jumper wire to battery power. 
An audible click should be heard and resistance on ohmmeter should drop to zero.

If relay does not click and resistance drops to zero, replace relay.

Horn Switch 

 With Air Bag 

 Removal and Installation 

 WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR BAG VEHICLE AND WHEN 
HANDLING AN AIR BAG. 

 WARNING: THE ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT NECESSARY FOR AIR BAG SYSTEM DEPLOYMENT IS 
POWERED DIRECTLY FROM THE BATTERY (10655) AND BACKUP POWER SUPPLY. TO AVOID 
ACCIDENTAL DEPLOYMENT AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY, THE BATTERY POSITIVE CABLE

 head retaining bolts and remove horn switch plates.

 (35-44 lb-in).

Section 13-07B: Compass

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Compass and Outside Temperature Display

 NOTE: The electronics within the instrument cluster (10849) are not 
serviceable. For a confirmed electronic failure, return the entire assembly to 
the manufacturer (packaged carefully to avoid damage to the vacuum fluorescent 
displays and other electronic components). Instrument cluster should be 
disassembled only to service plastic defects (refer to Section 13-01A ). 

Federal law requires that the odometer in any replacement 
speedometer/odometer must register the same mileage as that registered on the 
removed speedometer/odometer. Service replacement speedometer/odometers and 
odometer modules with the mileage preset to actual vehicle mileage are 
available through Ford Authorized Service Centers. In nearly all instances, 
the mileage continues to accumulate in the odometer memory even if the 
odometer does not display mileage. This mileage can usually be verified by the 
electronic service centers. Contact the service center for instructions to 
receive a replacement speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the mileage 
preset to actual mileage.

If the actual vehicle mileage cannot be verified, the service center 
will supply a speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the odometer 
display preset to zero ("0") miles and the service odometer segment ("s") 
illuminated in the vicinity of the odometer display. In addition, an odometer 
mileage sticker is supplied with the replacement odometer. This sticker must 
display the estimated vehicle mileage and is to be affixed to the driver door.

Section 13-07B: Compass

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Factors Affecting Accuracy 

 NOTE: Changes in vehicle direction are displayed only after vehicle direction 
has stabilized for at least two seconds.

The following factors may cause the compass to become temporarily 
inaccurate. The compass is designed to correct itself, but may take several 
days of normal driving. 

Magnetic mount devices (antennas, racks, etc.) should not be located on 
the roof of the vehicle because they affect compass accuracy. If these devices 
must be used, the compass must be recalibrated to accommodate them. 

Driving near power lines or objects with high iron or steel content 
(bridges, underground pipes and tunnels, etc.) may temporarily change the 
compass heading. The display should return to the true vehicle heading after 
the vehicle leaves the area. 

In most locations, magnetic north differs from the true north direction 
shown on maps. This difference, called magnetic variation, changes 
considerably across the country. Correct magnetic variation by performing the Compass Zone Adjustment 
 procedure outlined under Adjustments.

 NOTE: The compass module is mounted on the base of the inside rear view 
mirror (17700).

To remove the compass module, grab the front of the compass module and 
gently pull down. Press locking tang and remove connector from compass module.

Remove module.

ADJUSTMENTS

Compass Zone Adjustment

The zone setting is factory pre-set to Zone 8. Refer to the Compass Calibration 
Zone Map to verify the correct compass zone setting for your geographical location.

Press and hold reset button for four seconds until Current Zone Setting 
appears on the instrument cluster compass display.

Release the button.

Pressing the RH switch repeatedly will cycle the display through all 
possible zone settings. Stop cycling when the correct zone setting for your 
location is displayed.

Releasing the switch for five seconds will exit the zone setting mode.

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Calibration Adjustment

For optimum calibration, switch off all non-essential electrical 
accessories (including rear window defrost, heater/air conditioning, map 
lamps, wipers). Make sure all doors are shut.

Drive to an open, level area away from large metallic objects or 
structures.

Press and hold reset button on the compass for ten seconds until Circle Slowly appears 
on the instrument cluster compass display.

Release the reset button and drive slowly in a circle until CAL disappears 
from the display (about two to three circles).

The compass is now calibrated.

 Compass Calibration Zones 

[FIGURE: K23489B.gif]

Section 13-07B: Compass

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Vehicle Demagnetizing 

If after calibration the compass is still inaccurate, demagnetizing 
must be performed. 

The demagnetizing process requires the use of a demagnetizing coil 
commonly used by television service technicians to demagnetize television 
tubes. Demagnetize the vehicle by sweeping across the roof area over the 
compass with a demagnetizing coil as follows: 

 NOTE: Never turn demagnetizing equipment on or off within 1 meter (3 ft) of a 
vehicle's roof or the vehicle may be remagnetized. 

Standing 1 meter (3 ft) or more away from vehicle, turn on 
demagnetizing coil. 

 NOTE: Whenever the demagnetizing equipment is being operated over the 
vehicle's roof surface or within 1 meter (3 ft) of the vehicle, the operator 
must maintain a constant steady motion. Failure to do so may result in the 
vehicle being remagnetized. 

In one continuous motion, make four passes over roof of the vehicle. 
The demagnetizer should be held 25 mm (1 inch) or less away from (but not 
touching) the roof surface. 

After the fourth pass, without stopping the motion of demagnetizing 
coil, pull demagnetizer away from vehicle roof. 

When the demagnetizer coil is at least 1 meter (3 ft) away from 
vehicle, turn demagnetizing coil off. 

Perform compass Calibration Adjustment procedure as outlined. 

 Vehicle Demagnetizing

Section 13-08A: Indicator Lamp Module � Town Car

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Indicator Lamp Module 

The indicator lamp module system for Town Car consists of two separate 
modules. The modules are located below the instrument cluster to the left and 
right.

The left indicator lamp module consists of the following:

anti-lock brake system (ABS) indicator

left turn indicator

oil pressure indication system

anti-theft indicator

The right indicator lamp module consists of the following:

safety belt warning indicator

air bag warning indicator

right turn indicator

brake warning indicator

[FIGURE: K24145A.gif]

The indicator lamp module informs the driver when the following 
concerns exist:

oil pressure

air bag

anti-lock brake system

anti-theft system concern, or when system is armed

low brake fluid level, or when parking brake is engaged

Pinpoint Tests

PINPOINT TEST A: SAFETY BELT WARNING INDICATOR ALWAYS/NEVER ON

 A1 CHECK SAFETY BELT SWITCH INPUT 

Unbuckle driver safety belt. 

Using an ohmmeter connected to a known good ground, connect second lead 
lighting control module connector to Pin C2-17, Circuit 85 (BR/LB). 

Measure resistance. 

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

GO to A2 
 . 

SERVICE Circuit 85 (BR/LB) for open circuit. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST 
system. 

 A2 CHECK CIRCUIT 450 (DG/LG) OUTPUT AT LIGHTING CONTROL MODULE 

Using a voltmeter connected to a known good ground, connect test lamp 
probe to lighting control module connector Pin C3-8, Circuit 450 (DG/LG). 

Turn ignition switch to the RUN position. 

 Is B+ present?

Yes

No

GO to A3 
 . 

REPLACE lighting control module. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system. 

 A3 CHECK CIRCUIT 450 (DG/LG) INPUT AT RH INDICATOR PANEL 

Turn ignition key OFF. 

Connect voltmeter to RH indicator panel connector Pin 4, Circuit 450 
(DG/LG). 

Turn ignition switch to the RUN position. 

 Is B+ present?

Yes

No

REPLACE RH indicator panel. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

GO to A4 
 . 

 A4 CHECK CIRCUIT 450 (DG/LG) FOR OPEN 

Turn ignition switch OFF. 

Disconnect lighting control module. 

Using an ohmmeter, connect one lead to lighting control module 
connector Pin C3-8, Circuit 450 (DG/LG). Connect second lead to RH indicator 
panel connector Pin 4, Circuit 450 (DG/LG). 

Check continuity. 

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

REPLACE RH indicator panel. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 450 (DG/LG) for open circuit. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST 
system.

Yes

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Indicator Lamp Module 

 Removal 

Turn ignition switch to OFF. 

Gently insert a small, flat screwdriver into one of either access slots 
located on the vertical edges of the indicator lamp module bezel. 

Place a cloth pad between the screwdriver and the instrument panel 
(04320) to protect the finish. Gently pivot the screwdriver away from the 
indicator lamp module depressing the mounting tab toward the indicator lamp 
module. Apply a light outward force to free the end of the indicator lamp 
module from the instrument panel. Free other end of indicator lamp module with 
same procedure.

Pull indicator lamp module from instrument panel and disconnect 
connector. 

Repeat procedure for second indicator lamp module if required.

 Installation 

Connect instrument panel connector into indicator lamp module connector. 

Snap indicator lamp module into instrument panel opening.

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices � Chime System

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Electronic Instrument Cluster Tone 

With the ignition key in the RUN or ACC position, the safety belt 
warning chime in the lighting control module will emit a tone momentarily: 

when a button on the electronic instrument cluster (10849) is pushed. 

in conjunction with visual displays on the electronic instrument 
cluster. 

When ignition switch is in RUN or ACC, power is supplied through 
Circuit 296 (W/P) to lighting control module. 

When ignition switch is in RUN or START, power is supplied through 
Circuit 640 (R/Y) to lighting control module.

When appropriate, the electronic instrument cluster Circuit 183 (T/Y) 
sends a signal to activate the lighting control module causing the lighting 
control module to chime.
