Section 15-03: Speakers

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Radio Speakers 

Some vehicles are equipped with luxury radio speakers (18808).

Some vehicles may also be equipped with JBL® radio 
speakers.These speakers have "Ford/JBL® Audio System" 
printed on the magnet. 

JBL® radio speakers and luxury sound radio speakers 
are not interchangeable. However, the JBL® radio speakers 
used in the optional JBL® sound installations are removed 
and installed in the same manner as the premium radio speakers.

The JBL® system will also have a subwoofer radio 
speaker. The subwoofer is mounted on the rear deck between the rear speakers.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Subwoofer 

 JBL® System�Town Car 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove spare tire. 

Remove carpeted trim piece located on outboard side of luggage 
compartment (left of spare tire location) to expose subwoofer radio amplifier 
(18B849). 

Disconnect subwoofer amplifier power connector from the subwoofer. 

Remove subwoofer radio amplifier by removing mounting nut and sliding

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Phone, Mobile

The mobile phone system consists of these major components: 

headliner mounted mobile telephone microphone (19A391) with remote 
multi-function button 

glass mounted mobile telephone antenna (19A390) with multi-function 
control antenna cable (19A397)

mobile telephone transceiver (19A387)

mobile telephone handset (19A383)

Some features of the mobile phone system include: 

voice activation

hands-free operation

speed dialing of up to 30 numbers 

audio system muting during mobile phone operation

Section 15-04: Phone, Mobile

1996 Town Car Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification 

If there is a concern making calls on the mobile telephone, check the 
following information first. 

Make sure the telephone is turned ON. With the power button on, the 
system should be on while the ignition switch is in ACC or RUN. 

Make sure the customer is calling within the service area. NO SVC will 
appear in the display if the customer is calling from outside the service 
area. 

Check to see if the ROAM indicator is on. If so, follow the roaming 
instructions in the operating guide. 

Make sure the display does not read LOC'D. If it does, the phone must 
be unlocked using the customer's three-digit code. 

Make sure the mobile telephone handset (19A383) is securely cradled. 

Check the mobile telephone antenna (19A390) and mobile telephone power 
cable connections at the mobile telephone transceiver (19A387), located in the 
luggage compartment.

Check the handset modular connector. 

Check the telephone system registration. Also check to make sure that 
the telephone is properly programmed. Incorrect programming can result in 
single system scanning, loss of speed dialing, loss of hands-free audio, loss 
of auto redial, loss of dial tone multi-frequency tones, and the loss of other 
keypad/handset functions. 

Check the customer's account status with the cellular carrier. 

 System/Carrier Concerns 

Dropped calls, bad audio connections, noisy audio and other 
intermittent symptoms usually indicate a system or cellular carrier concern 
and are not concerns of the phone itself. Such symptoms may occur in 
situations similar to the following: 

in certain geographic areas (for example, excessive foliage, hills) or 
at the edge of service areas

at the same place each day

at the same time each day

under bridges, tunnels, in lower freeways and in congested downtown 
areas 

If the customer's phone exhibits any of the above symptoms or symptoms 
occur under the above conditions, the customer and/or the dealer should 
contact customer service at their particular cellular service provider/carrier 
or call the 1-800 service number provided in the Ford Cellular System Dealer 
kit. 

 Other Possible Concerns 

If for some reason the customer's electronic serial number was 
incorrectly recorded in the carrier switch, the phone will not work. Check 
programming procedure and confirm that the electronic serial number is 
recorded correctly with the local cellular carrier.

A customer's initial call must be made in his/her home service area for 
proper activation of the Ford Cellular System. 

A customer must wait until after 24 hours of the service activation 
before making a call from outside of his/her home service area or the phone 
might be reported stolen and service stopped. 

There may be a slight delay in activation after leaving dealership from 
initial delivery. 

The audio system does not work when the cellular phone is in use, this 
is because of the audio-mute feature which will mute the audio system when a 
call is placed or received. 

If, after checking these possibilities, the phone still does not 
function, do not attempt to service the phone. Call the cellular distributor 
Audiotronics at 1-800-755-4161.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Telephone Antenna

 NOTE: Use available Service Kit 18814 to replace mobile phone antenna.

 Removal 

Disconnect multi-function control antenna cable (19A397) from inner 
base of mobile telephone antenna (19A390).

Cut two-way tape retaining inner base to glass. To remove base, pull by 
hand. Do not pry on glass.

Remove radio antenna mast (18A886) from outer base of mobile telephone 
antenna.

Cut two-way tape retaining outer base to glass. To remove base, pull by 
hand. Do not pry on glass.

 Installation 

Clean two-way tape from inside and outside of glass.

Remove protective covering from two-way tape on inner base of mobile 
telephone antenna and attach antenna base to glass.

Connect multi-function control antenna cable to mobile telephone antenna.

Apply adhesive promoter meeting Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C to 
outside window glass and allow to dry before installing outer base of mobile 
telephone antenna. Proper use of adhesive and adhesive promoter ensures water 
resistant bond to glass.

Remove protective covering from two-way tape on outer base of mobile 
telephone antenna and attach antenna base to glass directly over inner base of 
mobile telephone antenna.

Install radio antenna mast to mobile telephone antenna.

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamps

 Aerodynamic 

The headlamp system consists of:

two aerodynamic headlamps (13008) with replaceable halogen bulbs

a multi-position headlamp switch (11654)

headlamp dimmer switch (part of multi-function switch (13K359))

lighting control module

circuit wiring and circuit protection

Power is supplied to the headlamps through lighting control module 
Circuit 502 (GY) and circuit protection C in the fuse junction panel. Ground 
is provided to the headlamp bulb and retainer (13N021) through Circuit 57 (BK).

Rotating the headlamp switch to the full clockwise position provides a 
signal to the lighting control module which provides power to the headlamp 
dimmer switch in the multi-function switch.

With the headlamp dimmer switch in the neutral position, power is 
supplied to the low-beam elements.

With the headlamp dimmer switch in the high beam position (forward 
detent), power is supplied to the high-beam elements and to the high-beam 
indicator in the instrument cluster (10849).

Momentarily pulling the headlamp dimmer switch toward the steering 
wheel (3600) closes the flash-to-pass switch and the high-beam headlamps 
light. They will remain lit until the headlamp dimmer switch is released.

 Headlamp Delay System�Autolamp 

The autolamp system:

provides light sensitive automatic on-off control of the lamps normally 
controlled by the regular headlamp switch. 

provides for increased visibility for occupants when leaving the 
vehicle by keeping the lamps on for a preselected period of time after the 
ignition switch is turned OFF. 

The preselected time lapse can be adjusted by the vehicle operator up 
to approximately three minutes. 

The system consists of:

a light sensitive light sensor amplifier (13A018)

lighting control module

a time delay switch that is part of the headlamp switch

For the autolamp system to be operational, the headlamp switch must be 
rotated counterclockwise from the OFF position. An autolamp indicator lamp 
will light when the lamps are energized by the autolamp system. 

In normal operation: 

the system will turn the exterior lamps on when the light available to 
the light sensor amplifier decreases below a predetermined level, such as at 
sunset. 

the lamps will automatically turn off when the level of outside light 
exceeds a predetermined level, such as during daylight hours. 

The system light sensor amplifier:

is mounted under a group of slotted holes in the defroster grille 
panel, left of the steering column. 

must always be exposed to outside light to function properly. 

 NOTE: Do not place any items over the slotted holes in the defroster grille 
panel left of the steering column which may block light to the light sensor 
amplifier and cause erratic operation of the system. 

The time delay switch, which is part of the headlamp switch operates as 
follows:

The time delay is functional when the headlamp switch is rotated 
counterclockwise from the OFF position. 

Maximum delay (three minutes) is obtained when the headlamp switch is 
rotated to the full counter-clockwise position.

The lighting control module is located under the instrument panel, to 
the right of the steering column, under the lower steering column cover. 

 Security Lighting 

The security lighting function provides exterior lighting as follows:

System operates when the ambient light available to the light sensor 
amplifier is below a predetermined level.

The system, like the illuminated entry system, may be activated three 
ways:

any button on the keyless entry keypad (14A626) is pressed,

any outside door handle is lifted, or

the UNLOCK button on the keyless entry remote transmitter is pressed.

The lighting control module will turn on parking lamps, tail lamps and 
headlamps on after a momentary delay if it is dark outside.

Lamps will remain on for approximately 25 seconds.

Security lighting turns off with the autolamp delayed exit function.

Whenever the LOCK button on the keyless entry remote transmitter is 
pressed:

parking lamps and tail lamps will flash momentarily.

the horn will chirp.

 Daytime Running Lamps 

Refer to Section 17-04 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamp Switch

The headlamp switch (11654) is a multi-position switch.

Rotating the headlamp switch clockwise to the PARK position (first 
detent) supplies a signal to the lighting control module which powers the 
front parking lamp (13200), the rear lamp (13404), the rear side marker lamps 
and the license lamp. Ground is provided to these lamps through Circuit 57 (BK).

Rotating the headlamp switch clockwise to the HEAD position (second 
detent) supplies a signal to the lighting control module which powers the 
headlamp dimmer switch which is part of the multi-function switch (13K359) as 
outlined under Headlamps.

Rotating the headlamp switch counterclockwise operates the autolamp and 
time delay systems as outlined under Headlamps.

Pressing in on the headlamp switch operates the dome lights. Refer to 
 Section 17-02 .

[FIGURE: K24220A.gif]

 Panel Dim Switch 

The panel dim switch is located above the headlamp switch and controls 
the instrument panel (04320) lighting intensity. Refer to Section 13-00 .

[FIGURE: K24221A.gif]

 Headlamps ON Warning Chime 

If the headlamp switch is left in either the PARK or HEAD position, and 
the driver door is opened, the lighting control module will chime.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Stoplight Switch

The stoplight switch (13480) provides power to the stoplamps and 
signals various other systems, including:

anti-lock brake control module (2B373)

powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650)

shift lock actuator (3Z719)

speed control servo

Power is provided to the stoplight switch through fuse 16 (15A). This 
fuse is hot at all times. With the stoplight switch closed, power is provided 
to the stoplamps through Circuit 511 (LG). Ground is provided to the stoplamps 
through Circuit 57 (BK).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Stoplamps

Stoplamps are mounted in the same housings as the rear lamps (13404).

Stoplamp functions are performed by double filament bulbs: 

The low power filaments are dedicated to the rear lamp operation and 
are continuously on when the headlamp switch is in PARK. 

Stoplamp function lights the high power filaments when the driver 
applies the brake pedal.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Backup 

The backup lamp system consists of:

transmission range (TR) sensor

the backup lamp below the rear lamp (13404), or in the rear reflector

circuit wiring and circuit protection

power is supplied to the transmission range (TR) sensor through fuse 1 
(15A) for Town Car or Fuse 5 (15A) for Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis. This 
fuse is hot in RUN. With the transmission in REVERSE, the switch closes and 
power is provided to the backup lamp bulbs on Circuit 140 (BK/PK). Ground is 
provided to the backup lamp bulbs through Circuit 57 (BK).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps 

The turn signal system consists of:

lighting control module.

multi-function switch (13K359).

turn signal miniature bulbs (13465).

turn signal indicators in the instrument cluster (10849).

circuit wiring and circuit protection.

Power is supplied to the lighting control module through instrument 
panel fuse 1 (15A). This fuse is hot in RUN. The lighting control module is 
connected to the turn signal switch of the multi-function switch. Ground is 
provided to the lighting control module and the turn signal miniature bulbs 
through Circuit 57 (BK).

Turn signal functions are performed by double filament bulbs in lamp 
assemblies located next to the headlamps. The turn/hazard function uses the 
second filament of the appropriate bulb(s).

With the multi-function switch in the right turn position, power is 
supplied to the RH front and rear turn signal miniature bulbs and the right 
turn indicator in the instrument cluster.

With the multi-function switch in the left turn position, power is 
supplied to the LH front and rear turn signal miniature bulbs and the left 
turn indicator in the instrument cluster.

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hazard Warning Flasher Switch

The hazard warning flasher switch (part of multi-function switch) is 
located on the top of the steering column tube (3514) forward of the steering 
wheel (3600).

The switch should cycle smoothly from OFF to ON by pressing and 
releasing the switch top.

The switch should produce an audible click when it toggles from one 
state to another.

The switch should extend markedly further above the column when the 
switch is ON than it does when it is OFF.

When the hazard switch is in the ON position, the four turn signal 
lamps should be flashing. Also, the two turn indicators in the instrument 
cluster (10849) should be flashing simultaneously.

Trailer Towing Package Wiring

a wiring feed, located under the instrument panel, for a trailer brake 
control unit

Refer to Section 18-01 for trailer towing package wiring information 
and diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Headlamps (With Autolamps)

Verify the customer's concern by operating the headlamps (with 
autolamps) to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged light sensor amplifier.

Damaged headlamp switch.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Blown fuse(s). Town Car:

 Fuse Junction Panel: 15 (15A), 6 (10A)
Circuit breaker 12 (20A).

 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis

 Fuse Junction
Panel Fuse: 4 (15A), 13 (15A), 6 (15A) Circuit breaker 12 (20A).

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data link connector 
(DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute 
Self Test Diagnostics for the Lighting Control Module as outlined in Section 18-04 . If, after performing data link diagnostic test, the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/ NOT EQUIPPED, go to Pinpoint Test
AA .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom
Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Lighting 
Control Module (LCM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index to continue 
diagnostics.

If the lighting control module cannot be accessed by the New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test
AA .

The Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) may 
also be used to diagnose this system.

DTC B1312: HEADLAMP INPUT SHORT TO BATTERY (+)

 B1312-1 CHECK SELF TEST 

Turn headlamp switch OFF.

Repeat self test.

 Is DTC B1312 retrieved?

Yes

No

GO to B1312-2 
 .

Headlamp switch was left in HEAD position during self test diagnostics. 
GO to next DTC.

 B1312-2 CHECK PID 

Access and disconnect headlamp switch connectors.

Access lighting control module PID HDLMPSW.

 Does PID indicate switch ON?

Yes

No

GO to B1312-3 
 .

REPLACE headlamp switch. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 B1312-3 CHECK CIRCUIT 1033 (R/Y) 

Access and disconnect lighting control module connector C1.

Using voltmeter connected to good ground, measure voltage at Pin C1-10, 
Circuit 1033 (R/Y).

 Is battery voltage present?

Yes

No

SERVICE short to battery in Circuit 1033 (R/Y). RESTORE vehicle. RETEST 
system.

REPLACE lighting control module. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

DTC B1317: BATTERY VOLTAGE HIGH

 B1317-1 MONITOR BATTERY VOLTAGE 

Clear DTC.

Using a voltmeter, monitor battery voltage during whole test.

Rerun self test. Be sure that no switches are pressed during test.

 Does voltage rise above 17 volts during test?

Yes

No

GO to Section 14-00 to SERVICE charging system concern.

GO to B1317-2 
 .

 B1317-2 TEST WITH ENGINE RUNNING 

Repeat Step B1317-1 with engine running.

 Does voltage rise above 17 volts during test?

Yes

No

GO to Section 14-00 to SERVICE charging system concern.

GO to B1317-3 
 .

 B1317-3 CHECK FOR DTC B1317 

Repeat Step B1317-1 .

 Is DTC B1317 still present?

Yes

No

REPLACE lighting control module. RETEST system.

System operating normally. NOTE that continuous DTC would have been set 
if the battery voltage rose above 17 volts for more than 2 minutes at any time.

DTC B1318: BATTERY VOLTAGE LOW

 B1318-1 MONITOR BATTERY VOLTAGE 

Clear DTC.

Using a voltmeter, monitor battery voltage during whole test.

Rerun self test. Be sure that no switches are pressed during test.

 Does voltage fall below 7 volts during test?

Yes

No

GO to Section 14-00 to SERVICE charging system concern.

GO to B1318-2 
 .

 B1318-2 TEST WITH ENGINE RUNNING 

Repeat Step B1318-1 with engine running.

 Does voltage fall below 7 volts during test?

Yes

No

GO to Section 14-00 to SERVICE charging system concern.

GO to B1318-3 
 .

 B1318-3 CHECK FOR DTC B1318 

Repeat Step B1318-1 .

 Is DTC B1318 still present?

Yes

No

REPLACE lighting control module. RETEST system.

System operating normally. NOTE that continuous DTC would have been set 
if the battery voltage dropped below 7 volts for more than 2 minutes at any 
time.

DTC B1342: ECU INTERNAL FAILURE

 B1342-1 SERVICE OTHER DTCs 

Diagnose and service all remaining DTCs.

After all other DTCs are serviced, repeat lighting control module self 
test.

 Did DTC B1342 return?

Yes

No

REPLACE lighting control module. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

Vehicle working properly.

DTC B1689: AUTOLAMP DELAY CIRCUIT FAILURE

 B1689-1 RERUN TEST 

Clear DTC.

Turn autolamps ON.

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Perform On-Demand self test.

 Is DTC B1689 still present?

Yes

No

GO to B1689-3 
 .

GO to B1689-2 
 .

 B1689-2 ENSURE THAT SWITCH IS NOT BAD 

Cycle Autolamp switch to maximum and off several times.

Perform On-Demand self test.

 Is DTC B1689 back?

Yes

No

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 217 (DB/O) for intermittent open. RETEST system.

 B1689-3 CHECK SWITCH 

Disconnect headlamp switch.

Set autolamp switch on minimum delay time (with autolamp on).

Using an ohmmeter, check resistance between headlamp switch terminals 
C2-9 and C2-1.

 Is resistance less than 5 ohms?

Yes

No

GO to B1689-4 
 .

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

 B1689-4 CHECK FOR SHORTED SWITCH 

Using an ohmmeter, check for short between headlamp switch terminals 
C2-9 and C2-1.

 Is resistance greater than 5 ohms?

Yes

No

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 217 (DB/O) for short to ground.

DTC B1692: AUTOLAMP DELAY SHORT TO GROUND

 B1692-1 RERUN TEST 

Clear DTCs.

Turn Autolamps ON.

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Retrieve continuous DTCs as outlined in Section 18-04 .

 Is DTC B1692 still present?

Yes

No

GO to B1692-3 
 .

GO to B1692-2 
 .

 B1692-2 CHECK FOR INTERMITTENT CONCERN 

Cycle Autolamp switch to maximum and off several times.

Retrieve continuous DTCs as outlined in Section 18-04 .

 Is DTC B1692 retrieved?

Yes

No

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

CHECK Circuit 217 (DB/O) for intermittent open circuit. RETEST system.

 B1692-3 CHECK HEADLAMP SWITCH 

Remove headlamp switch.

Set autolamp switch on minimum delay time (with autolamp on).

Using an ohmmeter, check for continuity between terminals C2-9 and C2-1 
on headlamp switch.

 is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

GO to B1692-4 
 .

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

 B1692-4 CHECK FOR SHORTED SWITCH 

Using an ohmmeter, measure resistance between terminals C2-9 and C2-7 
on headlamp switch.

 Is resistance greater than 5 ohms?

Yes

No

REPLACE headlamp switch. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 217 (DB/O) for short to ground.

 Is B+ present?

Inspection and Verification�Stoplamps

Verify the customer's original concern by operating the brake pedal to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged multi-function switch.

Damaged stoplight switch.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Blown fuse.

Fuse junction panel Fuse 16 (15A), Fuse 1 (15A), Fuse 5 (15A), Circuit
breaker 12 (20A).

Damaged connectors.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the 
symptom(s) and go to the Symptom Chart.

PINPOINT TEST BA: STOPLAMPS/REAR-MOUNT LAMPS INOPERATIVE

 BA1 TEST STOP LAMPS 

Press stoplight switch.

Check stop lamps and rear high mount lamp.

 Are all lamps on?

Yes

No

System operating properly.

GO to BA2 .

 BA2 TEST INDIVIDUAL LAMPS 

Press stoplight switch.

Check stop lamps and rear high mount lamp.

 Is any one lamp out?

Yes

No

SERVICE bulb or circuit specific to that bulb. RETEST system.

GO to BA3 .

 BA3 TEST REAR HIGH MOUNT LAMPS 

Press stoplight switch.

Check stoplamps and rear high mount lamp.

 Are only the rear high mount lamps on?

Yes

No

GO to BA5 .

GO to BA4 .

 BA4 TEST LAMPS 

Press stoplight switch.

Check stoplamps and rear high mount lamp.

 Are all lamps out?

Yes

No

GO to BA7 .

CHECK fuse 16 (15A) Town Car,1 (15A) Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis. If 
fuse is good, GO to BA5 .

 BA5 TEST CIRCUIT 511 (LG) VOLTAGE 

While holding stoplight switch, test for voltage on multi-function 
switch Pin C1-9, Circuit 511 (LG).

 Is voltage reading B+?

Yes

No

GO to BA6 .

SERVICE Circuit 511 (LG). RETEST system.

 BA6 TEST MULTI-FUNCTION SWITCH 

Disconnect multi-function switch C1 connector.

Using a jumper wire, short Pin C1-9, Circuit 511 (LG) to Pin C1-2, 
Circuit 5 (O/LB) Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis or Pin C1-10, Circuit 9 (LG/O) 
Town Car.

 Do stoplamps turn on?

Yes

No

REPLACE multi-function switch. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 5 (O/LB) and/or 9 (LG/O). RETEST system.

 BA7 TEST STOPLIGHT SWITCH INPUT 

Using a voltmeter, test for voltage at Circuit 10 (LG/R) to stoplight 
switch.

 Is B+ present?

Yes

No

GO to BA8 .

SERVICE Circuit 10 (LG/R) to stoplight switch. RETEST system.

 BA8 TEST STOPLIGHT SWITCH OUTPUT 

Using a voltmeter, test for voltage at output of stoplight switch 
Circuit 511 (LG).

Press stoplight switch. 

 Is voltage reading B+ at the switch?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 511 (LG). RETEST system.

REPLACE stoplight switch. RETEST system.

PINPOINT TEST BB: STOPLAMPS/REAR-MOUNT LAMPS ON CONTINUOUSLY

 BB1 CHECK STOPLAMP SWITCH OPERATION 

 NOTE: Verify stoplight switch is adjusted properly.

operation.

 Did stoplight switch operate properly?

Yes

No

GO to BB2 .

REPLACE damaged stoplight switch. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 BB2 CHECK CIRCUIT 511 (LG)

 Did stoplamps turn off?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 511 (LG) for short to B+. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Turn Signal Lamps/Hazard 
Flasher Lamps

Verify the customer's concern by operating the turn signal/hazard 
flasher lamps to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged multi-function switch.

Damaged indicator flasher.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Blown fuse.

Bulb burned out.

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data link connector 
(DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute 
Self Test Diagnostics for the Lighting Control Module as outlined in Section 18-04 . If, after performing data link diagnostic test, the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/ NOT EQUIPPED, go to Pinpoint Test
CA .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Lighting 
Control Module (LCM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index to continue 
diagnostics.

If the lighting control module cannot be accessed by the New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test
CA .

The Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) may 
also be used to diagnose this system.

DTC B1873: TURN SIGNAL/HAZARD POWER FEED SHORT TO GROUND

 B1873-1 RERUN TEST 

Verify that all switches are off and ignition switch is in RUN.

Clear DTC.

Perform On-Demand self test.

 is DTC B1873 still present?

Yes

No

GO to B1873-3 
 .

GO to B1873-2 
 .

 B1873-2 CHECK SWITCH 

Read PID FLSHPWR.

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Toggle hazard switch several times.

 Does PID show that flasher power is present at all times, except 
momentarily while switch is between states?

Yes

No

System operating normally.

REPLACE multi-function switch. RETEST system.

 B1873-3 CHECK SWITCH PID 

Read PID FLSHPWR.

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

 Does PID show that power is on?

Yes

No

REPLACE lighting control module. RETEST system.

GO to B1873-4 
 .

 B1873-4 CHECK CIRCUIT 385 (W/R) 

Turn hazard switch ON.

Read PID FLSHPWR.

 Does PID show that power is on?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 298 (P/O) to multi-function switch. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 385 (W/R) from multi-function switch to lighting 
control module. RETEST system.

PINPOINT TEST CA: NO COMMUNICATION WITH LIGHTING CONTROL MODULE

 CA1 CHECK CIRCUIT 195 (T/W) FOR POWER 

Disconnect lighting control module connector C3.

Using a voltmeter, measure for voltage at lighting control module 
connector Pin C3-6, Circuit 195 (T/W).

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to CA5 
 .

GO to CA2 
 .

 CA2 CHECK CIRCUIT 195 (T/W) FOR SHORT TO GROUND 

Remove Fuse 4 (15A) from fuse junction panel.

Using an ohmmeter connected to ground, measure resistance at lighting 
control module connector Pin C3-6, Circuit 195 (T/W).

 Is resistance less than 10K ohms?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 195 (T/W) for short to ground. REPLACE Fuse 4 (15A). 
RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

GO to CA3 
 .

 CA3 CHECK SUPPLY TO FUSE 4 (15A) 

Remove Fuse 4 (15A) from fuse junction panel.

Using a voltmeter, measure for voltage at Fuse 4 input cavity.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to CA4 
 .

SERVICE supply to Fuse 4 (15A). RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 CA4 CHECK CIRCUIT 195 (T/W) FOR OPEN 

Using an ohmmeter, measure resistance of Circuit 195 (T/W) between 
lighting control module connector Pin C3-6 and output cavity of Fuse 4.

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

REPLACE Fuse 4 (15A). RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 195 (T/W) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 CA5 CHECK CIRCUIT 54 (LG/Y) FOR POWER 

Disconnect lighting control module connector C3.

Using a voltmeter, measure for voltage at lighting control module 
connector Pin C3-11, Circuit 54 (LG/Y).

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to CA9 
 .

GO to CA6 
 .

 CA6 CHECK CIRCUIT 54 (LG/Y) FOR SHORT TO GROUND 

Remove Fuse 8 (15A) from fuse junction panel.

Using an ohmmeter connected to ground, measure resistance at lighting 
control module connector Pin C3-11, Circuit 54 (LG/Y).

 Is resistance less than 10K ohms?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 54 (LG/Y) for short to ground. REPLACE Fuse 8 (15A). 
RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

GO to CA7 
 .

 CA7 CHECK SUPPLY TO FUSE 8 (15A) 

Remove Fuse 8 (15A) from fuse junction panel.

Using a voltmeter, measure for voltage at Fuse 8 input cavity.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to CA8 
 .

SERVICE supply to Fuse 8 (15A). RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 CA8 CHECK CIRCUIT 54 (LG/Y) FOR OPEN 

Using an ohmmeter connected to ground, measure resistance of Circuit 54 
(LG/Y) between lighting control module connector Pin C3-11 and output cavity 
of Fuse 8.

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

REPLACE Fuse 8 (15A). RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 54 (LG/Y) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 CA9 CHECK LOGIC GROUND FOR OPEN 

Using an ohmmeter connected to ground, measure resistance at lighting 
control module connector Pin C3-9, Circuit 676 (PK/O) Town Car or Circuit 57 
(BK) Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis.

 Is resistance less than 5 ohms?

Yes

No

GO to Communication Network diagnostics in Section 18-04 to diagnose 
network concern.

SERVICE Town Car Circuit 676 (PK/O) or Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 
Circuit 57 (BK) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

PINPOINT TEST CB: TURN SIGNAL LAMPS/HAZARD FLASHER LAMPS INOPERATIVE

 CB1 TEST TURN SIGNALS 

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Test both left and right turn signals.

 Do turn signals flash at a normal rate?

Yes

No

System operating normally.

GO to CB2 .

 CB2 TEST FLASHER OPERATION 

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Test both left and right turn signals.

 Does one (or both) turn signals flash at a fast rate?

Yes

No

REPLACE damaged bulbs. If condition still exists, SERVICE Circuit 9 
(LG/O), 5 (O/LB), 3 (LG/W), 2 (W/LB) from multi-function switch to bulb and 
ground socket.

GO to CB3 .

 CB3 TEST INDIVIDUAL FLASHERS 

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Test both left and right turn signals.

 Does only one side flash?

Yes

No

SERVICE multi-function switch.

GO to CB4 .

 CB4 TEST FLASHERS 

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Test both left and right turn signals.

 Do both sides fail to flash?

Yes

No

CHECK Fuse 1 (15A) Town Car or Fuse 5 (15A) Crown Victoria, Grand 
Marquis. Fuse should have power in RUN. If fuse is good, GO to CB6 .

GO to CB5 .

 CB5 TEST FLASHER POWER 

Connect Rotunda New Generation Star Tester 007-00500 or equivalent to 
data link connector.

With ignition switch in RUN, read PID FLSHPWR.

 Does PID indicate flasher power?

Yes

No

GO to CB4 .

GO to CB3 .

 CB6 TEST HAZARD POWER�SWITCH ON 

Turn hazard switch ON.

Use Rotunda New Generation Star (NGS) Tester to read PID FLSHPWR.

 Does PID indicate flasher power?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 385 (W/R) from multi-function switch to lighting 
control module. GO to CB7 .

SERVICE open in Circuit 298 (P/O) from fuse junction panel to 
multi-function switch or multi-function switch. RETEST system.

 CB7 TEST FLASHER OUTPUT 

Remove lighting control module connector C3.

Using a jumper wire, short Pin C3-13 to Pin C3-15.

Turn hazard switch on.

 Are any of the turn signal bulbs illuminated?

Yes

No

REPLACE lighting control module. RETEST system.

GO to CB8 .

 CB8 ISOLATE LIGHTING CONTROL MODULE 

Remove lighting control module connector C3.

Turn on hazard flashers.

 Do any of the bulbs illuminate?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 44 (LB) from lighting control module to multi-function 
switch for short to B+. RETEST system.

GO to CB9 .

 CB9 TEST HAZARD FLASHERS 

Turn hazard flashers on.

 Do hazard flashers work?

Yes

No

System operating normally.

CHECK Fuse 16 (15A) Town Car or Fuse 1 (15A) Crown Victoria, Grand 
Marquis. If fuse is good, GO to CB10 .

 CB10 TEST PID POWER 

Connect Rotunda New Generation Star Tester 007-00500 or equivalent to 
data link connector.

With hazard switch on, read PID FLSHPWR.

 Does PID indicate flasher power?

Yes

No

GO to CB12 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Cornering Lamps

Verify the customer's concern by operating the cornering lamps to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged multi-function switch.

Damaged headlamp switch.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Bulb burned out.

Damaged Fuse: Fuse junction panel Fuse 4 (15A), Fuse 13 (15A), Circuit
breaker 12 (20A).

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the 
symptom(s) and go to the Symptom Chart.

Pinpoint Tests�Cornering Lamps

PINPOINT TEST DA: CORNERING LAMPS INOPERATIVE

 DA1 CHECK SUPPLY AT MULTI-FUNCTION SWITCH 

Gain access to multi-function switch connector C2.

Actuate headlamp switch to the HEAD position.

Using voltmeter connected to a known good ground, check Pin C2-2 
Circuit 502 (GY)-Town Car, Circuit 13 (R/BK)-Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to Pinpoint Test DB .

GO to DA2 .

 DA2 CHECK SUPPLY TO HEADLAMP SWITCH 

Gain access to headlamp switch connector C2.

Using voltmeter check Circuit 221 (O/W) Town Car or 195 (T/W) Crown 
Victoria, Grand Marquis at Pin C2-7 for voltage.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

REPLACE damaged headlamp switch. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 221 (O/W) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

PINPOINT TEST DB: INDIVIDUAL CORNERING LAMP INOPERATIVE

 DB1 CHECK MULTI-FUNCTION SWITCH OUTPUT 

Actuate multi-function switch to the left turn position.

Using voltmeter check Circuit 380 (P/Y) Pin C1-7 at multi-function 
switch connector.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

LEAVE multi-function switch actuated. GO to DB2 .

REPLACE multi-function switch. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 DB2 CHECK CIRCUIT 380 (P/Y) 

Gain access to cornering lamp miniature bulb.

Disconnect miniature bulb as outlined.

Using voltmeter check Circuit 380 (P/Y) for voltage.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to DB4 .

GO to DB3 .

 DB3 CHECK CIRCUIT 380 (P/Y) FOR SHORT 

Disconnect multi-function switch C1 connector.

Using an ohmmeter connected to a known good ground, connect second lead 
to multi-function switch connector Pin C1-7, Circuit 380 (P/Y).

Measure resistance.

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 380 (P/Y) for short. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 380 (P/Y) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 DB4 CHECK CIRCUIT 379 (BR/W) AT MULTI-FUNCTION SWITCH 

Actuate multi-function switch to the right turn position.

Using voltmeter check Circuit 379 (BR/W) Pin C1-3 at multi-function 
switch connector.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to DB5 .

REPLACE multi-function switch. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 DB5 CHECK CIRCUIT 379 (BR/W) FOR VOLTAGE 

Gain access to cornering lamp miniature bulb.

Disconnect miniature bulb as outlined.

Using voltmeter check Circuit 379 (BR/W) for voltage.

 Is voltage B+?

Yes

No

GO to DB7 .

GO to DB6 .

 DB6 CHECK CIRCUIT 379 (BR/W) FOR SHORT 

Disconnect multi-function switch C1 connector.

Using an ohmmeter connected to a known good ground, connect second lead 
to multi-function switch connector Pin C1-3, Circuit 379 (BR/W).

Measure resistance.

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

SERVICE Circuit 379 (BR/W) for short. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

SERVICE Circuit 379 (BR/W) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

 DB7 CHECK CIRCUIT 57 (BK) 

Using an ohmmeter connected to a known good ground, connect second lead 
to Circuit 57 (BK) at bulb socket.

Measure resistance at each lamp socket. 

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

REPLACE damaged cornering lamp miniature bulb. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST 
system.

SERVICE Circuit 57 (BK) for open. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Parking Lamps

Verify the customer's concern by operating the parking lamps to 
duplicate the concern.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged headlamp switch.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Bulb burned out.

Damaged connector.

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily serviced, 
correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If a concern remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent connected to the data link connector 
(DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute 
Self Test Diagnostics for the Lighting Control Module as outlined in Section 18-04 . If, after performing data link diagnostic test, the New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/ NOT EQUIPPED, go to Pinpoint Test
EA .

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Lighting 
Control Module (LCM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index to continue 
diagnostics.

If the lighting control module cannot be accessed by the New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test
EA .

The Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) may 
also be used to diagnose this system.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bulb, Exterior Illumination

 Removal and Installation 

 NOTE: Make sure appropriate lamp switch is off.

Refer to appropriate lamp Removal and Installation procedure to access 
bulb(s).

Two types of bulb sockets are used for most exterior illumination:

Standard plastic socket

Three-tab type

To remove the plastic socket assembly, turn the socket counterclockwise 
to the stop and remove the socket.

Pull miniature bulb (13465) straight out of socket.

To install, align miniature bulb and push straight into socket.

Index the smallest tab for locating the socket and rotate the socket 
clockwise to the stop.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Switch

 Removal and Installation 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove light switch knob (11666) from headlamp switch (11654) by 
grasping knob and pulling out.

Remove instrument panel finish panel (044D70) from instrument panel 
(04320). Refer to Section 01-12 .

Disconnect main wiring (14401) connector from headlamp switch.

Remove nut retaining headlamp switch to headlamp switch bracket 
(11A668) and remove switch.

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten switch retaining nut to 3 Nm
 (26 lb-in).

slotted, it is not necessary to remove the brake master cylinder push rod and 
one spacer washer from the brake pedal pin.

rod and the nylon washers and bushing away from the brake pedal. Remove the 
stoplight switch by sliding the stoplight switch up/down as required to remove.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Bulb 

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE HEADLAMP 
BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR THE HEADLAMP BULB AND 
RETAINER (13N021) IS DROPPED. HANDLE HEADLAMP BULB CAREFULLY. GRASP HEADLAMP 
BULB AND RETAINER ONLY BY ITS PLASTIC BASE. AVOID TOUCHING GLASS ENVELOPE. 
KEEP HEADLAMP BULB AND RETAINER OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. 

 NOTE: A properly aimed headlamp (13008) normally does not need to be re-aimed 
after installation of a headlamp bulb and retainer. A burned-out headlamp bulb 
and retainer should not be removed from the headlamp until just before a 
replacement headlamp bulb and retainer is to be installed. Removal of a 
headlamp bulb and retainer for an extended period of time may allow 
contaminants (dust, moisture, smoke) to enter the headlamp body and affect the 
performance of the headlamp. When servicing the headlamp bulb and retainer, 
energize the headlamp bulb and retainer only while it is contained within the 
headlamp body. 

Make sure headlamp switch (11654) is in off position. 

Lift hood and locate headlamp bulb and retainer installed in rear of 
headlamp. 

Remove headlamp dash panel junction wire (14290) from headlamp bulb and 
retainer by grasping wires firmly and snapping connector downward. 

Remove headlamp bulb and retainer by rotating counterclockwise (when 
viewed from rear) about one-eighth turn. 

Carefully remove headlamp bulb and retainer from socket in headlamp 
bulb (13007) by gently pulling straight out of socket. Do not rotate headlamp 
bulb and retainer during removal.

[FIGURE: K15986B.gif]

 Installation 

Insert the glass envelope of headlamp bulb and retainer into headlamp 
bulb while aligning the locking tabs. 

Rotate headlamp bulb and retainer one-quarter turn. 

Push headlamp dash panel junction wire into rear of headlamp bulb and 
retainer until it snaps and locks into position. 

Turn headlamp switch to HEAD position and check for proper operation. 
Close hood.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Lamp, Rear Hi-Mount

 Town Car 

 Removal 

Remove two screws (one each side) that hold the rear hi-mount lamp 
(13A613) to the package tray trim panels (46668). 

Lift the forward edge and pull rear hi-mount lamp slightly away from the 
back window glass (42006). 

Twist the bulb sockets to remove from the rear hi-mount lamp. 

Remove rear hi-mount lamp. 

Pull the miniature bulbs (13465) straight out of the socket.

 Installation 

Push new miniature bulbs into sockets. Install bulb sockets. 

Position the rear hi-mount lamp to the mounting brackets while aligning 
the locating pins on the bottom of the rear hi-mount lamp to the package tray 
trim panel. 

Lightly hold the rear hi-mount lamp toward the back window glass and 
install the two screws. 

Tighten screws to 1.4-2.3 Nm (12-20 lb-in). 

 Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 

 Removal 

Remove two screws retaining rear hi-mount lamp to adjustable mounting 
brackets. 

Lift up the rear hi-mount lamp and disconnect the wiring connector. 

Remove the two screws and adjustable mounting brackets from the 
replacement rear hi-mount lamp. The brackets that are installed from the old 
rear hi-mount lamp can be used again. 

If a miniature bulb (13466) needs to be replaced, pull miniature bulb 
out of the socket assembly.

 Installation 

Install miniature bulb to socket. Connect the wiring connector to the 
replacement rear hi-mount lamp. 

Position the rear hi-mount lamp over the mounting brackets. 

Lightly hold the rear hi-mount lamp toward the back window and install 
the two screws and tighten to 1.4-2.3 Nm (12-20 lb-in).

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp 

Perform headlamp aim adjustments with Rotunda Headlight Aimer 196-00001 
or equivalent. To aim the aerodynamically styled headlamps, the adjustable 
aimer adapters provided in the kit must be used. Adjustment aimer adapter 
positions are moulded into the bottom edge of the headlamp lens. Headlamps can 
be adjusted from inside the engine compartment by rotating the adjusting screw 
by hand using a hex-head socket. 

Set and lock the adjustable adapters, attach each adapter to its 
mechanical aimer, and aim headlamps per latest instructions in the kit. All 
headlamp adjustments should be made with a half-full fuel tank, plus or minus 
3.785 liter (one gallon), the vehicle unloaded, the luggage compartment empty 
(except for the spare tire and jacking equipment) and recommended pressure in 
all the tires. 

The equipment in Rotunda Headlamp Aimer 196-00001 or equivalent can be 
calibrated to accommodate a slight slope in the floor, making it usable almost 
any place in the garage. However, area must be reasonably flat.

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Courtesy 

Courtesy lamps can be turned on by using the dome lamp switch located 
on the headlamps switch assembly or by opening any door. A theater lighting 
feature gradually increases the light intensity ON and OFF when switched by 
opening or closing a door.

Courtesy lamps (controlled by the lighting control module) are 
activated by using the dome lamp switch (instant ON/OFF response) or when a 
door is ajar. The following lamps illuminate for courtesy lighting:

driver's and passenger's front door courtesy lamps 

driver's and passenger's rear door courtesy lamps 

instrument panel courtesy lamps (LH and RH)

front map lamps (LH and RH)

rear reading lamps (LH and RH)

driver's and passenger's door lock cylinder lamps

Operation is as follows:

Demand lighting includes courtesy lamps that are illuminated by the 
customer by directly or indirectly actuating a switch. 

The front map lamps are located in the overhead console. 

Each lamp is controlled by its own switch. 

The rear reading lamps are located on the upper side rail (one on each 
side). 

Each lamp is controlled by its own switch.

The following five demand lamps are provided with battery positive 
voltage (B+) vehicle system voltage by the demand lighting 
output of the lighting control module. The glove compartment, vanity, luggage 
compartment and engine compartment lamps have a dedicated switch that closes 
to ground to illuminate the lamp.

The following lamps are also part of the courtesy lighting function:

front map lamps (LH and RH)

rear reading lamps (LH and RH)

The front map lamps are powered by either the demand lighting circuit 
or the courtesy lighting circuit, depending upon the position of the switch 
associated with each lamp. 

When the customer turns the RH front map lamp switch ON, the front map 
lamp is illuminated through power supplied by the lighting control module 
demand lighting circuit. 

If the customer moves the map lamp switch to the OFF position, the 
power from the lighting control module demand lighting circuit is interrupted, 
and the lamp is reconnected to the courtesy lighting circuit.

The rear map lamps are powered by either the courtesy lighting circuit 
or the demand lighting circuit. 

When the rear reading lamp switch is moved to the ON position, the rear 
reading lamp is illuminated through power supplied by the lighting control 
module demand lighting circuit. 

If the rear reading lamp switch is moved to the OFF position, the power 
from the lighting control module demand lighting circuit is interrupted, and 
the lamp is reconnected to the courtesy lighting circuit.

 Door 

The door curb lamps are part of the courtesy lamp functions. The curb 
lamps illuminate when a door is opened or the headlamp switch is actuated to 
dome position.

 Foot 

Interior lamps (13776) are mounted on the lower closeout panels at both 
ends of the instrument panel (04320). The miniature bulbs (13466) are 
accessible from under the instrument panel. 

 Underseat 

The underseat lamps are part of the courtesy lamp functions. The lamps 
are retained with screws to the seat frame.

 Luggage Compartment 

The luggage compartment lamp (13A756): 

is mounted in the underside of the luggage compartment door (40110) 
(Town Car).

is mounted beneath package tray (Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis). 

illuminates when the luggage compartment door is opened and the battery 
saver feature is not active. 

 Lamp, Luggage Compartment 

[FIGURE: K16173E.gif]

The Town Car luggage compartment lamp housing contains a mercury switch 
that closes the lamp circuit when the luggage compartment door is opened. 

The Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis mercury switch is located near driver 
side hinge on underside of luggage compartment door.

 Engine Compartment 

The engine compartment lamp is mounted near the center of the hood 
(16612). 

The engine compartment lamp housing contains a mercury switch that 
closes the lamp circuit when the hood is opened. 

 Glove Compartment 

The glove compartment lamp system consists of: 

a glove compartment lamp switch and wire (14413) and miniature bulb 
assembly. 

circuit wiring and circuit protection. 

Opening the glove compartment door (06024) closes the switch which 
provides power to the glove compartment lamp switch and wire. The glove 
compartment lamp switch and wireis grounded to the sheet metal in the 
instrument panel. 

 Vanity Mirrors 

The vanity mirror lamp system consists of:

a switch and miniature bulb assembly in each inside visor (04100).

circuit wiring and circuit protection. 

Power is provided to the vanity mirror lamp switches through Circuit 53 
(BK/LB). Turning on the switch in the inside visor provides power to the lamps 
(13550).

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Illuminated Entry 

The illuminated entry system:

is controlled by the lighting control module. 

provides courtesy lighting upon entry to and exit from the vehicle.

The courtesy lamps illuminate when the driver's or passenger's front 
door handle is raised and the ignition switch is not in RUN or ACC. The 
keyless entry keypad: 

illuminates when the driver's or passenger's front door handle is 
raised, regardless of the ignition switch position. 

remains illuminated for five seconds after an outside door handle is 
raised, or for five seconds following the last keypad switch press.

Courtesy lamps will be illuminated for 25 (±1) 
seconds which includes a theater lighting ramp-up time (two seconds). This 
time interval does not include the theater lighting ramp-down time. Courtesy 
lamps will be extinguished before the 25 (±1)-second 
timeout if the ignition switch is turned to the RUN or ACC position.

The illuminated entry system has the following additions to accommodate 
the keyless entry system:

 NOTE: When the illuminated entry feature is activated by using the remote 
transmitter, the keyless entry keypad does NOT illuminate.

Pressing any switch on the keyless entry keypad (14A626) will also 
activate the illuminated entry system (with theater ramp-up). When the driver 
door module detects a switch press, it momentarily changes the status of the 
illuminated entry signal to a logic "low", commanding the lighting control 
module to activate the courtesy lamps. The keyless entry keypad will remain 
illuminated for five seconds following the illuminated entry "ON" signal 
transition or for five seconds following the last keypad switch press.

If the last two keyless entry keypad switches are pressed concurrently 
(to lock the doors), the lighting control module will turn off the lamps by 
sensing the all doors lock signal. The driver door module will also turn OFF 
the keyless entry keypad illumination when the last two keyless entry keypad 
switches are pressed concurrently.

The illuminated entry system has the following additions to accommodate 
the remote keyless entry feature:

Pressing the UNLOCK switch on the remote transmitter will also activate 
the illuminated entry function (with theater ramp-up). When the driver door 
module receives the UNLOCK command from the remote transmitter, it momentarily 
changes the status of the illuminated entry signal to a logic "low". This 
commands the lighting control module to activate the courtesy lamps for 25 (±
1) seconds.

Pressing the LOCK switch on the remote transmitter will turn OFF the 
courtesy lamps. When the driver door module receives the LOCK command from the 
remote transmitter, it issues a pulse on the all doors lock wire commanding 
the lighting control module to turn OFF the courtesy lamps.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Battery Saver

Battery saver prevents excessive drain from loads inadvertently left 
on. When the ignition switch is turned OFF, power is interrupted to the 
courtesy lamps (after a 10-minute timeout), the demand lamps (after a 
30-minute timeout) and headlamps (after a 10-minute timeout).

 BATTERY SAVER INPUTS AND OUTPUTS

Inputs

Outputs

Luggage compartment door ajar switch

Dome lamp switch

Front door handle switches

Hood open switch

Ignition switch status

Illuminated entry signal

Keyless entry keypad

Keyless entry remote transmitter

Luggage compartment

 door release

Courtesy lamps

Demand lamps

Headlamps

When the ignition switch is turned to OFF, the courtesy lamps interrupt 
timer and demand lamps interrupt timer begin their timeout. The interrupt 
timer is a feature of the lighting control module. Power is available to the 
lamps during timeout. At the end of the 9-11 minute timeout period, the 
lighting control module disables power to the courtesy lamps. At the end of 
the 25-35 minute timeout period, the lighting control module disables power to 
the demand lamps. The following lamps are affected:

Courtesy Lamps

Demand Lamps

Front door courtesy lamps

Rear reading lamps

Instrument panel courtesy lamps

Front map lamps

Rear door courtesy lamps

Door lock cylinder lamps

Glove compartment lamp

Vanity lamps

Luggage compartment lamp

Engine compartment lamp

Rear map lamps

Front map lamps

Turning the ignition switch to ACC or RUN will terminate the battery 
saver feature by disabling the interrupt timers and reinstating power to the 
lamps.

A reset event will set the courtesy lamps interrupt timer to zero. The 
reset events for the courtesy lamps interrupt timer are as follows:

turning ON the courtesy lamps via the dome lamp switch

detecting a change in state in the illuminated entry signal (from 
either the door handles or the driver's door module)

opening any door (as detected by the interior lamp switches)

A reset event will set the demand lamps interrupt timer to zero. The 
reset events for the demand lamps interrupt timer are as follows:

opening the hood (on Town Car only)

opening the luggage compartment door

detecting a change in state in the illuminated entry signal (from 
either the door handles or the driver door module)

opening any door (as detected by the interior lamp switches)

When the PANIC button on a keyless entry remote transmitter is pressed, 
or an anti-theft violation occurs, the panic alarm or anti-theft alarm 
function will override the courtesy lamps, demand lamps and headlamps battery 
saver functions for the duration of the alarm. Refer to Section 13-11 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Courtesy Lamps

Verify the customer's concern by operating the interior lamps (13776) 
to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged interior lamps.

Damaged switches.

Stuck switches.

Open fuses.

Damaged miniature bulbs.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Connectors damaged/corroded.

If the inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily 
serviced, correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and 
Verification.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New 
Generation (NGS) Tester 007-00500 or equivalent, connected to the data link 
connector (DLC) to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to 
execute Self Test Diagnostics for the lighting control module as outlined in 
 Section 18-04 . 

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom
Chart to continue diagnosis.

If diagnosis trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to Lighting Control 
Module (LCM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index to continue diagnosis.

If the lighting control module cannot be accessed by the NGS go to Pinpoint Test AA 
 .

control module connector Pin C3-8.

 Is resistance less than 10 K ohms?

No

 B1322-3 CHECK DRIVER DOOR AJAR SWITCH

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification�Illuminated Entry

Verify the customer's concern by operating the illuminated entry system 
to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Outside door handles.

Fuses 8 (15A) and circuit breaker 14 (20A).

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged driver's door module.

If the inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily 
serviced, correct the concern before continuing with Inspection and 
Verification.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, use Rotunda New 
Generation (NGS) Tester 007-00500, connected to the data link connector (DLC) 
to retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and to execute Self 
Test Diagnostics for the lighting control module and driver door module as 
outlined in Section 18-04 . 

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to Symptom Chart to continue diagnosis.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to Lighting 
Control Module (LCM) Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) Index.

If the lighting control module and driver door module can not be 
accessed by the NGS go to Pinpoint Test
BA for lighting control module or go 
to Pinpoint Test BB for Driver Door Module.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bulb 

 Removal and Installation 

Remove lens cover, if equipped, as outlined. 

Remove bulb by one of the following methods:

For twist-in bulbs, gently grasp the bulb, push lightly while turning 
counterclockwise and remove the bulb.

For pressure-fit bulbs, gently grasp bulb, pull the bulb straight out 
of contacts. If bulb gives resistance a screwdriver may be used under one edge 
for leverage.

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Lamp, Dome/Map Combination�Town Car and Grand Marquis

 Lens, Map Lamp 

 Removal 

Rotate interior lamp lens (13734) to stop. 

Insert thin-bladed screwdriver in slot on side of interior lamp lens 
and twist screwdriver to pop off interior lamp lens. 

[FIGURE: K14610B.gif]

Remove miniature bulb (13466) by pulling it out of socket. 

 Installation 

Install new miniature bulb into socket. 

Position interior lamp lens to interior lamp (13776) (interior lamp 
lens will only fit one way) and push to snap in interior lamp. 

 Housing 

 Removal 

Rotate both interior lamp lenses to stop, then continue to push until 
interior lamp goes beyond stop and is in the vertical position. 

Disengage plastic locking retainers on both ends of interior lamp while 
pulling interior lamp away from roof headlining (51916). 

[FIGURE: K14609B.gif]

Disconnect wiring connector. 

Insert thin flat-bladed screwdriver in slots and release locking tabs 
on ends of retainer while pulling downward. 

[FIGURE: K14611B.gif]

Squeeze sides of retainer inward and remove retainer through opening in 
roof headlining.

 Installation 

Install retainer through hole in roof headlining. 

Position locking tabs to holes in sheet metal and push to snap in. 

Connect wiring connector. 

Position interior lamp to locking retainers (only fits one way) and push 
interior lamp to snap in. 

Rotate lamp interior lamp lenses to the flat (horizontal) position.

Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 

 Lens, Dome Lamp 

 Removal and Installation

(13734) from the interior lamp (13776).

To install, snap interior lamp lens back into interior lamp.

 Removal and Installation 

Remove the three screws that retain the interior lamp to its mounting 
surface. 

Lower the courtesy/map lamp bracket (13763).

Carefully pry out center section of courtesy/map lamp bracket.

Remove two retaining screws.

Disconnect electrical connector. Remove interior lamp.

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Lamp, Glove Compartment 

 Removal and Installation 

The glove compartment lamp switch and wire (14413) is mounted above the 
glove compartment (06010). The glove compartment lamp switch and wire also 
functions as the lock striker. 

Disconnect wiring.

Remove one screw retaining glove compartment lamp switch and wire to 
instrument panel (04320). 

To install, place interior lamp (13776) in position, install retaining 
screw and adjust glove compartment door latch (06072) to striker position. 
Tighten screw to 2-3 Nm (18-26 lb-in). 

To replace miniature bulb (13466), pull out with thumb and finger. 
Install new miniature bulb by pressing into socket.

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1996 Town Car, Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System

The daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the high-beam 
headlamps ON, with a reduced light output and without illuminating the 
high-beam indicator in the instrument panel, when the following conditions are 
met:

Ignition switch is in the RUN position.

Park brake is fully released.

Headlamp switch (11654) is in the OFF or PARK position.

 NOTE: If vehicle is equipped with an automatic lighting system, the DRL 
system is active until the automatic system turns on the headlamps (13008).

The DRL system is required by the Canadian government for vehicles sold 
in Canada. 

 WARNING: DRL CONTROL MODULE GETS VERY HOT DURING OPERATION. BE SURE DRL CONTROL 
MODULE HAS COOLED BEFORE HANDLING IT. 

The DRL system uses a DRL control module and bracket assembly on the 
radiator support (16138) at the center of vehicle.

The wiring is connected to theheadlamp dash panel junction wire 
(14290). The DRL output consists of rapidly pulsating short bursts of power 
which cannot be measured using most multimeters. Daytime running lamp control 
output cannot be adjusted.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer's concern by following these steps:

Turn ignition switch OFF.

Turn headlamp switch (11654) to HEAD position.

Check low beam headlamp operation.

Turn high beam headlamp ON with dimmer switch.

Check high beam operation.

Turn high beam headlamps OFF.

Turn low beam headlamps OFF.

Check high beam indicator located in instrument cluster for proper 
concern.

If any concerns are noted with regular headlamp operation, refer to 
 Section 17-01 to diagnose.

Check daytime running lamps system operation:

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Check for high beam headlamps ON at reduced intensity.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged lamps.

Open fuse junction panel Fuse 15 (15A), 7 (15A), Town Car or 12 (20A),
5 (15A) Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis.

Damaged connectors.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged ignition switch.

Damaged DRL control module.

Damaged parking brake signal switch and bracket.

Power distribution box Fuse 12 (20A), Town Car or high beam headlamps
(20A), Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the 
symptom(s) and go to the Symptom Chart.

 Is resistance 5 ohms or less?

Yes

No

Town Car, GO to E3

Fuse Junction Panel 

The fuse junction panel (14A067):

contains most of the fuses and circuit breakers used in the vehicle. 

is a part of the instrument panel-to-dash panel wiring harness. 

cannot be replaced separately from the main wiring (14401). 

To remove the main wiring of which the fuse junction panel is a part, 
refer to wiring harness Removal and Installation as outlined. 

 Location 

The fuse junction panel is located to the left of the steering column.

To expose the fuse junction panel, remove instrument panel steering 
column cover (04459) as outlined in Section 01-12 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuse Links 

A fuse link is: 

a short length of insulated wire, integral with the engine compartment 
wiring harness. 

several wire gauges smaller than the circuit which it protects. 

generally located in-line directly from the alternator output circuit. 

 Fusible Links�Town Car 

[FIGURE: K24036A.gif]

 Fusible Links�Crown Victoria, Grand Marquis 

[FIGURE: K24037A.gif]

 NOTE: Replacement fuse link color coding may vary from production fuse link 
color coding. 

Production fuse links are color-coded: 

12 gauge: GY 

14 gauge: DG 

16 gauge: BK 

18 gauge: BR 

20 gauge: DB 

When heavy current flows, such as when a booster battery is connected 
incorrectly or when a short to ground occurs in the wiring harness, the fuse 
link burns out and protects the generator (GEN) (10346) or wiring. 

A burned out fuse link may have bare wire ends protruding from the 
insulation or it may have only expanded or bubbled insulation with illegible 
identification. 

When it is hard to determine if the fuse link is burned out, perform 
the continuity test.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Trailer Towing Package Wiring

Vehicles equipped with the trailer towing package have the following 
additions to support the trailer wiring:

The addition of a set of relays and connector (Town Car has two 
connectors) on the rear lamp wiring (14405) located in the rear driver side 
quarter panel.

The trailer feed wiring (13A576) is supplied with the vehicle and is 
installed at the time of pre-delivery.

Vehicles are equipped with a wiring feed, located under the instrument 
panel, for a trailer brake control unit.

 Trailer Wiring Relays 

The trailer wiring relays are located in the rear driver's side quarter 
panel area and are accessible through the luggage compartment. The relays are 
mounted to the relay mounting bracket (14A301).

[FIGURE: K22833A.gif]

 Trailer Wiring Feed Wiring 

The trailer feed wiring connects to the rear lamp wiring connector 
(Town Car has two connectors) located directly below the relay mounting 
bracket. The trailer feed wiring is routed along the interior of the luggage 
compartment and exits the luggage compartment.

 NOTE: Damage to the vehicle caused by installation of aftermarket components 
or service to trailer feed wiring by non-Ford authorized dealers is not 
covered by Ford Motor Company warranty.

A connector end matching the trailer to be towed is to be installed on 
the end of the trailer feed wiring. This installation should be done by a 
camper/trailer repair center.

The trailer end of the trailer feed wiring has the following feeds for 
trailer wiring:

 A1 CHECK LIGHTING OPERATION

 Does the exterior lighting system of vehicle operate properly?

Yes

No

 Town Car

 Are fuses OK?

Yes

No

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuse Junction Panel

 Removal and Installation 

 NOTE: The fuse junction panel (14A067) is a part of the instrument 
panel-to-dash panel main wiring (14401). The fuse junction panel cannot be 
replaced separately from the harness.

Remove the wiring harness, of which the fuse junction panel is a part, 
as outlined.

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Power Distribution Box

 Removal and Installation 

 WARNING: ALWAYS DISCONNECT THE BATTERY BEFORE SERVICING HIGH CURRENT FUSES IN 
POWER DISTRIBUTION BOX AND HARNESS (14516). 

 NOTE: Power distribution box and harness is part of headlamp dash panel 
junction wire assembly.

Remove battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect all wiring harness connectors with takeouts coming from 
power distribution box and harness. This includes:

one-way connections to starter motor relay.

four-way and three-way connectors to engine control sensor wiring 
assembly.

Remove two hex nuts retaining power distribution box to sheet metal and 
remove power distribution box and harness.

To install, reverse Removal procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuses

 WARNING: IN THE EVENT THAT THE AIR BAG DIAGNOSTIC MONITOR FUSE IS BLOWN, THE AIR 
BAG SYSTEM MUST BE DISARMED TO PREVENT INADVERTENT DEPLOYMENT OF THE AIR BAGS. 
REFER TO SECTION 01-20B FOR SERVICING OF THE AIR BAG SYSTEM BEFORE REPLACING 
THIS FUSE. (FUSE K TOWN CAR, FUSE 10 CROWN VICTORIA, GRAND MARQUIS.) 

To check or replace a fuse: 

 NOTE: If the fuse is mounted on the fuse junction panel (14A067), remove the 
instrument panel steering column cover (04459). Refer to Section 01-12 . 

Locate the blown fuse and remove it by pulling it out of its cavity (no 
special tools required). 

Replace the blown fuse with the same approved amp rating for that 
particular circuit. To install the new fuse, push straight in until the fuse 
seats itself fully in the cavity.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relay

 Removal and Installation 

 NOTE: Replace a defective relay (14N089) with one having the same part number 
and rating.

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Grasp inoperative relay and pull straight out of box.

To install, align blades of relay with socket and push in until relay 
is seated completely.

Restore vehicle.

Check operation of circuit controlled by relay.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Circuit Breakers

 Removal and Installation 

 NOTE: Always replace an inoperative relay (14N089) with one having the same 
part number and rating.

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Grasp inoperative circuit breaker and pull straight out of fuse 
junction panel (14A067).

To install, align blades of new circuit breaker with socket and push in 
until circuit breaker is seated.

Restore vehicle.

Check operation of circuit controlled by circuit breaker.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Indicator Flasher

Hazard indicator flasher (13350) is located on rear of instrument panel 
fuse junction panel (14A067). 

Turn indicator flasher is located on front of instrument panel fuse 
junction panel.

 Removal and Installation 

Pull indicator flasher straight out of fuse junction panel.

To install, align blades of indicator flasher with socket and push 
indicator flasher into fuse junction panel until seated.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wiring Harnesses 

 NOTE: The remaining illustrations in this Section show the complete wiring 
harness installation for these vehicles. Refer to the illustrations for the 
harness being replaced while performing the Removal and Installation 
procedures. 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Refer to Section 01-05 if it is necessary to remove any trim panels to 
gain access to the harness. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect all wiring harness connectors. 

Disengage harness from all locators, straps and/or clips as necessary, 
including ground wire eyelets. Remove harness from vehicle. 

 Installation 

Position harness in vehicle. Make sure that harness is engaged in all 
locators, straps and/or clips. 

Connect all harness connectors to components or other harnesses as 
necessary. 

Secure ground eyelets to body as necessary. 

Connect battery ground cable. Check all applicable circuits for proper 
operation. 

Install any trim removed during harness removal. Refer to Section 01-05 .

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Wire Terminals 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Wire Fitting Crimping Tool

T67S-17018-A

To remove an individual wire from its connector, use the following 
procedure: 

Remove the connectors from the dash panel, the fuse junction panel 
(14A067) or power distribution box. 

Release the retaining tang from the wire terminal with a narrow 
screwdriver and pull the wire and terminal out of the connector. 

If necessary, remove damaged terminal by cutting from wire.

Install new terminal to wire using instructions furnished with Wire 
Fitting Crimping Tool T67S-17018-A.

To install, push the terminal into the connector until the retaining 
tang snaps into the locking hole in the terminal. 

A new waterproof butt splice connector has been released that should be 
used on all service to wiring located in the engine compartment. 

The duraseal heat-shrinkable nylon splice provides a long-lasting 
splice that can withstand water, salt, condensation, corrosion and heat, all 
of which cause problems for conventional unsealed splices. 

The inner wall of the splice connector is lined with a special adhesive 
that melts as the splice is heated and flows under pressure from the tubing, 
filling voids and sealing the splice. 

The duraseal splice can be easily installed using a standard 
pre-insulated crimp tool and a heat gun. They are also color coded for easy 
identification of gauge sizes, yet are transparent for visual inspection of 
the finished splice. Refer to the following illustration for installation 
instructions. 

[FIGURE: K19462B.gif]

Part Name

Class

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Connectors, In-Line

 CAUTION: Raise locking tab just enough to release connector halves. If locking 
tab breaks, that connector half must be replaced for reliable repair. 

For connector with locking tab on one side only:

Insert a flat-blade screwdriver under locking tab and gently twist. 

Grasp wires and pull to separate. 

[FIGURE: K22479A.gif]

 CAUTION: Raise locking tabs just enough to release connector halves. If locking 
tab breaks, that connector half must be replaced for a reliable repair. 

For connector with locking tab on both sides:

Insert a flat-blade screwdriver under the locking tab and gently twist. 

Grasp wires and pull until locking tab is on the ramp. 

Turn connector over and repeat procedure on opposite side. 

Grasp wires and pull to separate. 

[FIGURE: K22480A.gif]

For connector with thumb release locking tab:

Place thumb under locking tab and push up. 

Grasp wires and pull to separate. 

[FIGURE: K22481A.gif]

For radio speaker connectors:

Insert a small flat-blade screwdriver into locking tang of electrical 
connector for radio speaker (18808) as shown in following illustration.

Move screwdriver to disengage locking tang and pull connector straight 
off radio speaker.

[FIGURE: K24394A.gif]

For connector with no tabs:

Grasp wires with both hands. 

Pull to separate. 

[FIGURE: K22483B.gif]
